translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 151
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 151

sentences.zh: 【梁紀七】　趙柔兆敦牂，盡強圉協洽，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Liang Records 7] Beginning with Rouzhao Dunxiang, ending with Qiangyu Xixie, two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Liang Records 7] Spanning from the year Rouzhao Dunxiang through Qiangyu Xixie—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝七普通七年（

translations.literal: The seventh year of Putong of Emperor Wu of the High Ancestor (
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Putong of Emperor Wu of the High Ancestor (

sentences.zh: 丙午，公元五二六年）

translations.literal: bingwu, A.D. 526)
translations.idiomatic: the year bingwu, A.D. 526)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑朔，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day of the month (xinchou), a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (xinchou), a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 壬子，魏以汝南王悅領太尉。

translations.literal: On renzi, Wei appointed the Prince of Runan, Yue, as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Northern Wei appointed the Prince of Runan, Yuan Yue, as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 魏安州石離、穴城、斛鹽三戍兵反，應杜洛周，眾合二萬，洛周自松岍赴之。

translations.literal: At An Province, the garrisons of Shili, Xuecheng, and Huyan—all three—rebelled and joined Du Luozhou; their forces totaled twenty thousand. Luozhou himself went from Songqin to join them.
translations.idiomatic: The garrisons at Shili, Xuecheng, and Huyan in An Province rose in revolt and rallied to Du Luozhou, mustering twenty thousand men in all; Luozhou marched from Songqin to join them.

sentences.zh: 行台常景使別將崔仲哲屯軍都關以邀之，仲哲戰沒，元譚軍夜潰，魏以別將李琚代譚為都督。

translations.literal: Commander of the Forward Army Chang Jing sent the detached general Cui Zhongzhe to encamp at Duguan Pass to intercept them. Zhongzhe was killed in battle, and Yuan Tan's army fled by night; Wei replaced Tan as commander with the detached general Li Ju.
translations.idiomatic: The forward-army commander Chang Jing stationed the detached general Cui Zhongzhe at Duguan Pass to block them; Zhongzhe fell in battle, Yuan Tan's army collapsed in a night rout, and Wei appointed the detached general Li Ju in Tan's place as commander.

sentences.zh: 仲哲，秉之子也。

translations.literal: Zhongzhe was the son of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhe was Cui Bing's son.

sentences.zh: 初，魏廣陽王深通於城陽王徽之妃。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Prince of Guangyang Shen of Wei had an affair with the consort of the Prince of Chengyang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Northern Wei Prince of Guangyang, Yuan Shen, had taken the consort of the Prince of Chengyang, Yuan Hui, as his lover.

sentences.zh: 徽為尚書令，為胡太后所信任；

translations.literal: Hui was Director of the Masters of Writing and was trusted by Empress Dowager Hu;
translations.idiomatic: Hui served as Director of the Masters of Writing and enjoyed the trust of Empress Dowager Hu;

sentences.zh: 會恆州人請深為刺史，徽言深心不可測。

translations.literal: when the people of Heng Province petitioned to have Shen made their governor, Hui said that Shen's intentions could not be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: when the people of Heng Province asked that Shen be made their governor, Hui warned that Shen's motives were impossible to read.

sentences.zh: 及杜洛周反，五原降戶在恆州者謀奉深為主，深懼，上書求還洛陽。

translations.literal: When Du Luozhou rebelled, the surrendered households of Wuyuan at Heng Province plotted to set Shen up as their leader. Shen was afraid and submitted a memorial asking to return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Luozhou rose in revolt, the Wuyuan surrendered households at Heng Province plotted to make Shen their leader; Shen, alarmed, memorialized the throne asking to be recalled to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 魏以左衛將軍楊津代深為北道大都督，詔深為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Wei appointed the Left Guard General Yang Jin to replace Shen as Grand Commander of the Northern Route and ordered Shen to take office as Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: Wei replaced Shen with the Left Guard General Yang Jin as grand commander of the northern route and appointed Shen Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 徽，長壽之孫也。

translations.literal: Hui was the grandson of Changshou.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was a grandson of Yuan Changshou.

sentences.zh: 五原降戶鮮于修禮等帥北鎮流民反於定州之左城，改元魯興，引兵向州城，州兵御之不利。

translations.literal: Xianyu Xiuli and others of the surrendered households of Wuyuan led the displaced people of the northern garrisons in revolt at Zuocheng in Ding Province, changed the era name to Luxing, and marched on the provincial capital; the provincial troops could not withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Xiuli and other leaders among the Wuyuan surrendered households rallied the northern-garrison refugees in revolt at Zuocheng in Ding Province, proclaimed the era name Luxing, and advanced on the provincial seat, which the local troops proved unable to hold back.

sentences.zh: 楊津至靈丘，聞定州危迫，引兵救之，入據州城。

translations.literal: Yang Jin reached Lingqiu, heard that Ding Province was in dire peril, led his troops to the rescue, and entered to hold the provincial city.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jin reached Lingqiu and learned that Ding Province was in grave danger, he marched to its relief and took possession of the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 修禮至，津欲出擊之，長史許被不聽，津手劍擊之，被走得免。

translations.literal: When Xiuli arrived, Jin wished to sally out and attack him, but the chief clerk Xu Bei would not consent; Jin struck at him with his own sword, and Bei fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuli arrived, and Jin wanted to lead a sortie against him, but his chief clerk Xu Bei refused; Jin drew his sword and struck at Bei, who fled and escaped injury.

sentences.zh: 津開門出戰，斬首數百，賊退，人心少安。

translations.literal: Jin opened the gates and gave battle, beheading several hundred; the rebels withdrew, and morale was somewhat restored.
translations.idiomatic: Jin opened the gates and fought, taking several hundred heads; the rebels fell back, and the defenders' spirits steadied somewhat.

sentences.zh: 詔尋以津為定州刺史兼北道行台。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward an edict appointed Jin governor of Ding Province and concurrently commander of the northern-route forward army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon followed appointing Jin governor of Ding Province and concurrently commander of the northern-route forward army.

sentences.zh: 魏以揚州刺史長孫稚為大都督北討諸軍事，與河間王琛共討修禮。

translations.literal: Wei appointed the governor of Yang Province, Changsun Zhi, grand commander of all armies for the northern punitive campaign, to join with the Prince of Hejian Chen in attacking Xiuli.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made the governor of Yang Province, Changsun Zhi, grand commander of the northern punitive forces and sent him with the Prince of Hejian, Yuan Chen, to suppress Xiuli.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲戌，北伐眾軍解嚴。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiaxu, the armies of the northern expedition stood down from alert.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiaxu, the northern expeditionary armies were stood down from alert.

sentences.zh: 魏西部敕勒斛律洛陽反於桑干西，與費也頭牧子相連結。

translations.literal: The Chile of the western regions of Wei, Hulu Luoyang, rebelled west of the Sanggan and joined forces with the Feiyetou chieftain Muzi.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Luoyang of the western Chile tribes in Wei rose west of the Sanggan River and allied with the Feiyetou chieftain Muzi.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲寅，游擊將軍爾朱榮擊破洛陽於深井，牧子於河西。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiayin, the mobile general Erzhu Rong defeated Luoyang at Shenjing and Muzi on the west bank of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiayin, the mobile general Erzhu Rong routed Luoyang at Shenjing and Muzi on the river's west bank.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙酉，臨川靖惠王宏卒。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yiyou, Prince Jinghui of Linchuan Hong died.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on yiyou, Prince Jinghui of Linchuan, Xiao Hong, died.

sentences.zh: 魏大赦。

translations.literal: Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，魏以侍中、車騎大將軍城陽王徽為儀同三司。

translations.literal: On guisi, Wei appointed the Palace Attendant and General of Chariots and Cavalry, the Prince of Chengyang Hui, as a peer of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Wei elevated the Palace Attendant and General of Chariots and Cavalry, the Prince of Chengyang Yuan Hui, to the rank of peer of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 徽與給事黃門侍郎徐紇共毀侍中元順於太后，出為護軍將軍、太常卿。

translations.literal: Hui and the Attendant at the Yellow Gate Xu He together slandered the Palace Attendant Yuan Shun before the empress dowager, and Shun was transferred out to be General Who Guards the Army and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and the Attendant at the Yellow Gate Xu He joined in slandering the Palace Attendant Yuan Shun before the empress dowager, and Shun was transferred out to serve as General Who Guards the Army and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 順奉辭於西遊園，紇侍側，順指之謂太后曰：「此魏之宰嚭，魏國不亡，此終不死！

translations.literal: Shun took his leave at the Western Tour Garden; He waited at his side. Shun pointed at him and said to the empress dowager, "This is Wei's Bo Pi—so long as Wei does not perish, this man will never die!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shun took his leave at the Western Tour Garden, He stood at his side; Shun pointed at him and told the empress dowager, "This is Wei's Bo Pi—as long as Wei does not fall, this man will never die!"

sentences.zh: 」紇脅肩而出，順抗聲叱之曰：「爾刀筆小才，正堪供幾案之用，豈應污辱門下，斁我彝倫！

translations.literal: He shrank his shoulders and slipped out. Shun shouted at him in a ringing voice, "You petty clerk with your brush and knife—fit only to serve at a desk! How dare you defile the gates below and corrupt our moral order!"
translations.idiomatic: He hunched his shoulders and slipped away; Shun thundered at him, "You petty clerk with your brush and knife—fit only to serve at a desk! How dare you pollute the gates below and corrupt our moral order!"

sentences.zh: 」因振衣而起。

translations.literal: With that he shook out his robes and rose.
translations.idiomatic: With that he shook out his robes and strode off.

sentences.zh: 太后默然。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said nothing.

sentences.zh: 魏朔州城民鮮于阿胡等據城反。

translations.literal: The townspeople of Shuozhou in Wei, Xianyu Ahu and others, seized the city and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Ahu and other townspeople of Shuozhou in Wei seized the city and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 杜洛周南出抄掠薊城，魏常景遣統軍梁仲禮擊破之。

translations.literal: Du Luozhou marched south to raid and plunder around Ji; Chang Jing of Wei sent the commander Liang Zhongli to defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Luozhou marched south to raid the region of Ji; Chang Jing of Wei sent the commander Liang Zhongli, who routed him.

sentences.zh: 丁未，都督李琚與洛周戰於薊城之北，敗沒。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the commander Li Ju fought Luozhou north of Ji and was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, the commander Li Ju fought Luozhou north of Ji, was defeated, and perished.

sentences.zh: 常景帥眾拒之，洛周引還上谷。

translations.literal: Chang Jing led the masses to resist him, and Luozhou withdrew to Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Jing led his forces to hold him off, and Luozhou withdrew to Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 長孫稚行至鄴，詔解大都督，以河間王琛代之。

translations.literal: Changsun Zhi reached Ye; an edict relieved him of the post of grand commander and replaced him with the Prince of Hejian Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Changsun Zhi reached Ye, an edict relieved him of the grand command and replaced him with the Prince of Hejian, Yuan Chen.

sentences.zh: 稚上言：「向與琛同在淮南，琛敗臣全，遂成私隙，今難以受其節度。

translations.literal: Zhi submitted a memorial: "Formerly Chen and I were together in Huainan; when Chen was defeated I preserved the army intact, and a private grudge arose between us. Now I find it hard to accept his command."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized the throne: "Chen and I once served together in Huainan; when he was defeated I preserved the army intact, and a private grudge arose between us. I cannot now accept his command."

sentences.zh: 」魏朝不聽。

translations.literal: The Wei court would not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei court would not listen.

sentences.zh: 前至呼沱，稚未欲戰，琛不從。

translations.literal: When they advanced to the Hutuo, Zhi did not wish to give battle, but Chen would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When they advanced to the Hutuo River, Zhi did not wish to fight, but Chen would not agree.

sentences.zh: 鮮于修禮邀擊稚於五鹿，琛不赴救，稚軍大敗，稚、琛並坐除名。

translations.literal: Xianyu Xiuli intercepted and struck Zhi at Wulu; Chen did not go to his rescue, and Zhi's army was utterly defeated. Both Zhi and Chen were stripped of their names and offices.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Xiuli ambushed Zhi at Wulu; Chen did not go to his rescue, and Zhi's army was shattered. Both Zhi and Chen were stripped of rank and office.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁未，魏主下詔將北討，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dingwei, the Wei sovereign issued an edict announcing a northern campaign; within and without, the realm was placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingwei, the Wei emperor issued an edict announcing a northern campaign, and the realm was placed on alert within and without.

sentences.zh: 既而不行。

translations.literal: In the end the campaign was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the campaign was never launched.

sentences.zh: 衡州刺史元略，自至江南，晨夕哭泣，常如居喪。

translations.literal: Yuan Lue, governor of Heng Province, from the time he reached the lands south of the Yangzi wept morning and evening as though in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lue, governor of Heng Province, had wept morning and evening like a man in mourning ever since he reached the lands south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 及魏元義死，胡太后欲召之，知略因刁雙獲免，征雙為光祿大夫，遣江革、祖□恆之南還以求略。

translations.literal: When Yuan Yi of Wei died, Empress Dowager Hu wished to summon Lue back and learned that Lue had been spared through Diao Shuang; she summoned Shuang to be Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and sent Jiang Ge and Zu Hengzhi south to bring Lue back.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Yi of Wei died, Empress Dowager Hu wished to recall Lue and learned that Lue had been spared thanks to Diao Shuang; she summoned Shuang as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and sent Jiang Ge and Zu Hengzhi south to negotiate Lue's return.

sentences.zh: 上備禮遣之，寵贈甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor prepared full rites for his departure and bestowed lavish favors and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent him off with full ceremony and lavished rich gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 略始濟淮，魏拜略為侍中，賜爵義陽王；

translations.literal: As soon as Lue crossed the Huai, Wei appointed him Palace Attendant and enfeoffed him as Prince of Yiyang;
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Lue crossed the Huai, Wei appointed him Palace Attendant and enfeoffed him as Prince of Yiyang;

sentences.zh: 以司馬始賓為給事中，栗法光為本縣令，刁昌為東平太守，刁雙為西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: he made Sima Shibin an Attendant at the Gates, Li Faguang magistrate of his home county, Diao Chang governor of Dongping, and Diao Shuang governor of Western Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: he made Sima Shibin an Attendant at the Gates, Li Faguang magistrate of his home county, Diao Chang governor of Dongping, and Diao Shuang governor of Western Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 凡略所過，一飧一宿皆賞之。

translations.literal: Everywhere Lue had passed, everyone who had given him a single meal or night's lodging was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who had given Lue so much as a meal or a night's lodging along the way was rewarded.

sentences.zh: 魏以丞相高陽王雍為大司馬。

translations.literal: Wei appointed the Chancellor, the Prince of Gaoyang Yong, as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed the Chancellor, the Prince of Gaoyang, Yuan Yong, as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 復以廣陽王深為大都督，討鮮于修禮；

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangyang Shen was again made grand commander to attack Xianyu Xiuli;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangyang, Yuan Shen, was again made grand commander to suppress Xianyu Xiuli;

sentences.zh: 章武王融為左都督，裴衍為右都督，並受深節度。

translations.literal: Rong of the Prince of Zhangwu was made left commander, Pei Yan right commander, and both were placed under Shen's command.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Zhangwu, Yuan Rong, was made left commander and Pei Yan right commander, both subordinate to Shen.

sentences.zh: 深以其子自隨，城陽王徽言於太后曰：「廣陽王攜其愛子，握兵在外，將有異志。

translations.literal: Shen took his son with him. The Prince of Chengyang Hui said to the empress dowager, "The Prince of Guangyang has brought his beloved son and holds troops abroad—he harbors ulterior designs."
translations.idiomatic: Shen took his son with him on campaign. The Prince of Chengyang Yuan Hui told the empress dowager, "The Prince of Guangyang has brought his beloved son and commands troops in the field—he intends treachery."

sentences.zh: 」乃敕融、衍潛為之備。

translations.literal: She then ordered Rong and Yan secretly to take precautions against him.
translations.idiomatic: She then secretly ordered Rong and Yan to guard against him.

sentences.zh: 融、衍以敕示深，深懼，事無大小，不敢自決。

translations.literal: Rong and Yan showed the edict to Shen; Shen was afraid, and in matters great and small he no longer dared decide on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Yan showed Shen the edict; Shen was terrified and no longer dared decide anything, great or small, on his own.

sentences.zh: 太后使問其故，對曰：「徽銜臣次骨，臣疏遠在外，徽之構臣，無所不為。

translations.literal: The empress dowager sent to ask the reason. He replied, "Hui bears a grudge against me to the bone. I am far away in the provinces, and in framing me Hui stops at nothing."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager sent to ask why; he replied, "Hui bears a grudge against me to the bone. I am far away in the provinces, and in framing me he stops at nothing."

sentences.zh: 自徽執政以來，臣所表請，多不從允。

translations.literal: "Since Hui took power, most of my memorial petitions have not been granted."
translations.idiomatic: "Since Hui took power, most of my memorial petitions have been denied."

sentences.zh: 徽非但害臣而已，從臣將士，有勳勞者皆見排抑，不得比它軍，仍深被憎嫉，或因其有罪，加以深文，至於殊死，以是從臣行者，莫不悚懼。

translations.literal: "Hui harms not only me: the officers and men who follow me—all who have merit are suppressed and cannot be treated like other armies; they are deeply hated and envied besides. Sometimes when one of them is guilty, Hui piles on charges until the penalty is death, so that everyone who marches with me is filled with dread."
translations.idiomatic: "Hui harms not only me: every officer and soldier who follows me with merit is suppressed and cannot be treated like other armies; they are hated and envied besides. When one of them is guilty, Hui piles on charges until the penalty is death, so that everyone who marches with me lives in dread."

sentences.zh: 有言臣善者，視之如仇讎；

translations.literal: "Whoever speaks well of me he treats like an enemy;"
translations.idiomatic: "Whoever speaks well of me he treats as an enemy;"

sentences.zh: 言臣惡者，待之如親戚。

translations.literal: "whoever speaks ill of me he treats like a kinsman."
translations.idiomatic: "whoever speaks ill of me he treats like kin."

sentences.zh: 徽居中用事，朝夕欲陷臣於不測之誅，臣何以自安！

translations.literal: "Hui holds power at court and day and night seeks to trap me in an unforeseen execution—how can I feel secure!"
translations.idiomatic: "Hui holds power at court and day and night seeks to trap me in an unforeseen execution—how can I feel secure!"

sentences.zh: 陛下若使徽出臨外州，臣無內顧之憂，庶可以畢命賊庭，展其忠力。

translations.literal: "If Your Majesty would send Hui out to govern an outer province, I would have no worry for what lies behind me and might then devote my life in the rebels' camp and display my loyal strength."
translations.idiomatic: "If Your Majesty would send Hui out to govern a distant province, I would have no worry for what lies behind me and might then devote my life in the rebels' camp and display my loyal strength."

sentences.zh: 」太后不聽。

translations.literal: The empress dowager would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager would not listen.

sentences.zh: 徽與中書舍人鄭儼等更相阿黨，外似柔謹，內實忌克，賞罰任情，魏政由是愈亂。

translations.literal: Hui and the Secretariat Gentleman Zheng Yan and others formed factions in turn; outwardly they seemed gentle and cautious, inwardly they were jealous and harsh, and rewards and punishments followed their whims—Wei government grew all the more chaotic thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and the Secretariat Gentleman Zheng Yan and others formed shifting factions; outwardly mild and cautious, inwardly jealous and harsh, they meted out rewards and punishments at whim, and Wei government grew all the more chaotic.

sentences.zh: 戊申，魏燕州刺史崔秉帥眾棄城奔定州。

translations.literal: On wushen, Cui Bing, governor of Yan Province in Wei, led his troops in abandoning the city and fled to Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Cui Bing, governor of Yan Province in Wei, abandoned his city and fled with his troops to Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，魏以安西將軍宗正珍孫為都督，討汾州反胡。

translations.literal: On yichou, Wei appointed the Anxi General Zongzheng Zhensun commander to suppress the rebel Hu of Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Wei appointed the Anxi General Zongzheng Zhensun commander to suppress the rebel Hu of Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 六月，魏降蜀陳雙熾聚眾反，自號始建王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Chen Shuangchi of the surrendered Shu of Wei gathered a host and rebelled, styling himself King of Shijian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Chen Shuangchi of the surrendered Shu in Wei gathered followers and rebelled, proclaiming himself King of Shijian.

sentences.zh: 魏以假鎮西將軍長孫稚為討蜀都督。

translations.literal: Wei appointed the acting General Who Pacifies the West Changsun Zhi commander for the Shu punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed the acting General Who Pacifies the West, Changsun Zhi, commander of the Shu punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 別將河東薛修義輕騎詣雙熾壘下，曉以利害，雙熾即降。

translations.literal: The detached general Xue Xiuyi of Hedong rode with light cavalry to Shuangchi's camp, explained advantage and harm, and Shuangchi surrendered at once.
translations.idiomatic: The detached general Xue Xiuyi of Hedong rode with light cavalry to Shuangchi's camp, explained the stakes, and Shuangchi surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 詔以修義為龍門鎮將。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Xiuyi garrison commander of Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Xiuyi garrison commander of Longmen.

sentences.zh: 丙子，魏徙義陽王略為東平王，頃之，遷大將軍、尚書令，為胡太后所委任，與城陽王徽相埒，然徐、鄭用事，略亦不敢違也。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Wei transferred the Prince of Yiyang Lue to be Prince of Dongping; shortly afterward he was promoted to Grand General and Director of the Masters of Writing, entrusted by Empress Dowager Hu and equal in standing to the Prince of Chengyang Hui—yet Xu and Zheng held power, and Lue did not dare defy them either.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Wei transferred the Prince of Yiyang, Yuan Lue, to be Prince of Dongping; shortly afterward he was promoted to Grand General and Director of the Masters of Writing, entrusted by Empress Dowager Hu and equal in standing to the Prince of Chengyang Yuan Hui—yet Xu He and Zheng Yan held power, and Lue did not dare defy them either.

sentences.zh: 杜洛周遣都督王曹紇真等將兵掠薊南。

translations.literal: Du Luozhou sent the commander Wang Cao Hezhen and others to lead troops in plundering south of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Du Luozhou sent the commander Wang Cao Hezhen and others to raid south of Ji.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙午，行台常景遣都督於榮等擊之於栗園，大破之，斬曹紇真及將卒三千餘級。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingwu, the forward-army commander Chang Jing sent the commander Yu Rong and others to strike them at Liyuan, inflicting a great defeat and beheading Cao Hezhen and more than three thousand officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on bingwu, the forward-army commander Chang Jing sent the commander Yu Rong and others to strike them at Liyuan, routing them and taking the heads of Cao Hezhen and more than three thousand officers and men.

sentences.zh: 洛周帥眾南趣范陽，景與榮等又破之。

translations.literal: Luozhou led his host south toward Fanyang; Jing and Rong and the others defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou led his host south toward Fanyang; Jing, Rong, and the others defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 魏僕射元纂以行台鎮恆州。

translations.literal: Yuan Zuan, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing in Wei, held Heng Province as forward-army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zuan, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing in Wei, held Heng Province as forward-army commander.

sentences.zh: 鮮于阿胡擁朔州流民寇恆州，戊申，陷平城，纂奔冀州。

translations.literal: Xianyu Ahu led the displaced people of Shuozhou in raiding Heng Province; on wushen he took Pingcheng, and Zuan fled to Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Ahu led the displaced people of Shuozhou in raiding Heng Province; on wushen he took Pingcheng, and Zuan fled to Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 上聞淮堰水盛，壽陽城幾沒，復遣郢州刺史元樹等自北道攻黎漿，豫州刺史夏侯但等自南道攻壽陽。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that the waters behind the Huai embankment were high and Shouyang was nearly submerged; he again sent Yuan Shu, governor of Ying Province, and others by the northern route to attack Lijiang, and Xiahou Dan, governor of Yu Province, and others by the southern route to attack Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard that the waters behind the Huai embankment were high and Shouyang was nearly submerged; he again sent Yuan Shu, governor of Ying Province, and others by the northern route against Lijiang, and Xiahou Dan, governor of Yu Province, and others by the southern route against Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸巳，賊帥元洪業斬鮮于修禮，請降於魏；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on guisi, the rebel leader Yuan Hongye beheaded Xianyu Xiuli and asked to surrender to Wei;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guisi, the rebel leader Yuan Hongye beheaded Xianyu Xiuli and offered to surrender to Wei;

sentences.zh: 賊黨葛榮復殺洪業自立。

translations.literal: the rebel Ge Rong then killed Hongye and set himself up in his place.
translations.idiomatic: but the rebel Ge Rong then killed Hongye and set himself up in his place.

sentences.zh: 魏安北將軍、都督恆、朔討虜諸軍事爾朱榮過肆州，肆州刺史尉慶賓忌之，據城不出。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong, General Who Pacifies the North and commander of all armies for the Heng-Shuo punitive campaign in Wei, passed through Si Province; the governor of Si Province, Wei Qingbin, was jealous of him and held the city without coming out.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong, General Who Pacifies the North and commander of the Heng-Shuo punitive campaign in Wei, passed through Si Province; the governor Wei Qingbin, jealous of him, shut the city and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 榮怒，舉兵襲肆州，執慶賓還秀容。

translations.literal: Rong was enraged, raised troops, and stormed Si Province, seizing Qingbin and taking him back to Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was enraged, raised troops, stormed Si Province, seized Qingbin, and took him back to Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 署其從叔羽生為刺史，魏朝不能制。

translations.literal: He appointed his father's younger brother Yusheng governor; the Wei court could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed his father's younger cousin Yusheng governor, and the Wei court could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 初，賀拔允及弟勝、岳從元纂在恆州，平城之陷也，允兄弟相失，岳奔爾朱榮，勝奔肆州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Heba Yun and his brothers Sheng and Yue had followed Yuan Zuan at Heng Province; when Pingcheng fell, the Yun brothers lost one another—Yue fled to Erzhu Rong and Sheng fled to Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Heba Yun and his brothers Sheng and Yue had followed Yuan Zuan at Heng Province; when Pingcheng fell the brothers were separated—Yue fled to Erzhu Rong and Sheng fled to Si Province.

sentences.zh: 榮克肆州。

translations.literal: Rong captured Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong captured Si Province,

sentences.zh: 得勝，大喜曰：「得卿兄弟，天下不足平也！

translations.literal: he obtained Sheng and said in great delight, "With you brothers in hand, the realm is not hard to pacify!"
translations.idiomatic: he obtained Sheng and said in delight, "With you brothers in hand, the realm is not hard to pacify!"

sentences.zh: 」以為別將，軍中大事多與之謀。

translations.literal: He made him a detached general, and on major affairs of the army he often took counsel with him.
translations.idiomatic: He made him a detached general and often consulted him on major affairs of the army.

sentences.zh: 九月，已酉，鄱陽忠烈王恢卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiyou, Prince Zhonglie of Poyang Hui died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiyou, Prince Zhonglie of Poyang, Xiao Hui, died.

sentences.zh: 葛榮既得杜洛周之從，北趣瀛州，魏廣陽忠武王深自交津引兵躡之。

translations.literal: Ge Rong, having taken over Du Luozhou's following, pressed north toward Ying Province; Shen, the Loyal Martial King of Guangyang in Wei, led troops from Jiaojin in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong, having absorbed Du Luozhou's following, pressed north toward Ying Province; the Loyal Martial King of Guangyang, Yuan Shen, led troops from Jiaojin in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，榮至白牛邏，輕騎掩擊章武莊武王融，殺之。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Rong reached Bainiu Luo and with light cavalry made a surprise attack on Rong, the Martial King of Zhangwu, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Ge Rong reached Bainiu Luo and with light cavalry surprised and killed the Martial King of Zhangwu, Yuan Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮自稱天子，國號齊，改元廣安。

translations.literal: Rong styled himself Son of Heaven, made his state name Qi, and changed the era name to Guang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong proclaimed himself Son of Heaven, named his state Qi, and adopted the era name Guang'an.

sentences.zh: 深聞融敗，停軍不進。

translations.literal: When Shen heard that Rong had been defeated, he halted his army and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen heard that Yuan Rong had been defeated, he halted his army and would not advance.

sentences.zh: 侍中元晏宣言於太后曰：「廣陽王盤桓不進，坐圖非望。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant Yuan Yan declared to the empress dowager, "The Prince of Guangyang lingers without advancing and sits plotting unlawful ambitions."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Attendant Yuan Yan told the empress dowager, "The Prince of Guangyang lingers without advancing and sits plotting unlawful ambitions."

sentences.zh: 有於謹者，智略過人，為其謀主，風塵之際，恐非陛下之純臣也。

translations.literal: "There is one Yu Jin whose wisdom and stratagems surpass others and who serves as his chief planner—in these troubled times I fear he is not Your Majesty's wholly loyal subject."
translations.idiomatic: "His chief planner Yu Jin surpasses others in wisdom and stratagem—in these troubled times I fear he is not Your Majesty's wholly loyal subject."

sentences.zh: 」太后深然之，詔榜尚書省門，募能獲謹者有重賞。

translations.literal: The empress dowager deeply agreed and issued an edict posted at the gate of the Masters of Writing office offering a heavy reward to whoever could capture Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed deeply and posted an edict at the gate of the Masters of Writing office offering a heavy reward for Jin's capture.

sentences.zh: 謹聞之，謂深曰：「今女主臨朝，信用讒佞，苟不明白殿下素心，恐禍至無日。

translations.literal: When Jin heard of it he said to Shen, "Now a woman rules the court and trusts slanderers and flatterers; if she does not understand Your Highness's true heart, I fear disaster will come any day."
translations.idiomatic: When Jin heard of it he told Shen, "A woman now rules the court and trusts slanderers and flatterers; if she does not understand Your Highness's true heart, disaster may come any day."

sentences.zh: 謹請束身詣闕，歸罪有司。

translations.literal: "I ask to bind myself and go to the palace to answer before the authorities."
translations.idiomatic: "I ask to surrender myself at court and answer before the authorities."

sentences.zh: 」遂徑詣榜下，自稱於謹；

translations.literal: He went straight to the posted notice and identified himself as Yu Jin;
translations.idiomatic: He went straight to the posted notice and identified himself as Yu Jin;

sentences.zh: 有司以聞。

translations.literal: the authorities reported it.
translations.idiomatic: the authorities reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太后引見，大怒。

translations.literal: The empress dowager summoned him and was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager summoned him and was furious.

sentences.zh: 謹備論深忠款，兼陳停軍之狀，太后意解，遂捨之。

translations.literal: Jin set forth in full Shen's loyal sincerity and also explained the circumstances of halting the army; the empress dowager's mind was eased, and she released him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin set forth Shen's loyal sincerity in full and explained why the army had halted; the empress dowager's anger eased, and she released him.

sentences.zh: 深引軍還，趣定州，定州刺史楊津亦疑深有異志；

translations.literal: Shen led his army back and hastened to Ding Province; Yang Jin, governor of Ding Province, also suspected that Shen harbored ulterior designs;
translations.idiomatic: Shen led his army back toward Ding Province, but Yang Jin, the governor, also suspected him of ulterior designs;

sentences.zh: 深聞之，止於州南佛寺。

translations.literal: when Shen heard of it he halted south of the province at a Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: when Shen heard of this he halted at a Buddhist temple south of the provincial seat.

sentences.zh: 經二日，深召都督毛謚等數人，交臂為約，危難之際，期相拯恤。

translations.literal: After two days Shen summoned the commander Mao Yi and several others, locked arms in covenant, and pledged that in times of peril they would rescue and succor one another.
translations.idiomatic: After two days Shen summoned the commander Mao Yi and several others, locked arms in covenant, and pledged that in times of peril they would rescue one another.

sentences.zh: 謚愈疑之，密告津，雲深謀不軌。

translations.literal: Yi grew all the more suspicious, secretly informed Jin, and said Shen was plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yi grew only more suspicious and secretly told Jin that Shen was plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 津遣謚討深，深走出，謚呼噪逐深。

translations.literal: Jin sent Yi to attack Shen; Shen fled, and Yi shouted and clamored in pursuit of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Shen fled, and Yi shouted and clamored in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 深與左右間行至博陵界，逢葛榮游騎，劫之詣榮。

translations.literal: Shen and his attendants made their way by hidden paths to the border of Boling, encountered Ge Rong's scouting horsemen, were seized, and taken to Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and his attendants stole away toward Boling, met Ge Rong's scouting horsemen, were seized, and brought before Rong.

sentences.zh: 賊徒見深，頗有喜者，榮新立，惡之，遂殺深。

translations.literal: Among the rebels who saw Shen, many were pleased, but Rong had only lately established himself and disliked this, so he killed Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Many rebels who saw Shen were pleased, but Rong, having only lately proclaimed himself ruler, took dislike to this and had Shen killed.

sentences.zh: 城陽王徽誣深降賊，錄其妻子。

translations.literal: The Prince of Chengyang Hui slandered Shen as having surrendered to the rebels and seized his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Chengyang Yuan Hui slandered Shen as a rebel collaborator and seized his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 深府佐宋游道為之訴理，乃得釋。

translations.literal: Song Youdao, an aide in Shen's princely establishment, pleaded his case, and they were released.
translations.idiomatic: Song Youdao, an aide in Shen's household, pleaded their case, and they were released.

sentences.zh: 游道，繇之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Youdao was a great-great-grandson of You.
translations.idiomatic: Youdao was a great-great-grandson of Song You.

sentences.zh: 甲申，魏行台常景破杜洛周，斬其武川王賀拔文興等，捕虜四百人。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the forward-army commander Chang Jing of Wei defeated Du Luozhou, beheaded his Prince of Wuchuan Heba Wenxing and others, and captured four hundred of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the forward-army commander Chang Jing of Wei defeated Du Luozhou, beheaded his Prince of Wuchuan Heba Wenxing and others, and took four hundred prisoners.

sentences.zh: 就德興陷魏平州，殺刺史王買奴。

translations.literal: Jiudexing took Ping Province of Wei and killed the governor Wang Mainu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiudexing captured Ping Province in Wei and killed the governor Wang Mainu.

sentences.zh: 天水民呂伯度，本莫折念生之黨也，後顯據顯親以拒念生；

translations.literal: Lu Bodu of Tianshui, originally a partisan of Moqi Niansheng, later seized Xianqin in display of force to resist Niansheng;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bodu of Tianshui had originally been a partisan of Moqi Niansheng, but later seized Xianqin to resist him;

sentences.zh: 已而不勝，亡歸胡琛，琛以為大都督、秦王，資以士馬，使擊念生。

translations.literal: before long he could not prevail, fled back to Hu Chen, and Chen made him grand commander and King of Qin, supplying him with troops and horses to attack Niansheng.
translations.idiomatic: before long he was defeated, fled back to Hu Chen, who made him grand commander and King of Qin and supplied him with troops and horses to attack Niansheng.

sentences.zh: 伯度屢破念生軍，復據顯親，乃叛琛，東引魏軍。

translations.literal: Bodu repeatedly defeated Niansheng's army, reoccupied Xianqin, then rebelled against Chen and drew Wei armies eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Bodu repeatedly defeated Niansheng's army, reoccupied Xianqin, then turned against Chen and invited Wei armies eastward.

sentences.zh: 念生窘迫，乞降於蕭寶寅，寶寅使行台左丞崔士和據秦州。

translations.literal: Niansheng was hard pressed and begged to surrender to Xiao Baoyin; Baoyin sent the forward-army Left Director Cui Shihe to hold Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Niansheng, hard pressed, begged to surrender to Xiao Baoyin, who sent the forward-army Left Director Cui Shihe to hold Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 魏以伯度為涇州刺史，封平秦郡公。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Bodu governor of Jing Province and enfeoffed him as Duke of Pingqin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Bodu governor of Jing Province and enfeoffed him as Duke of Pingqin.

sentences.zh: 大都督元修義停軍隴口，久不進。

translations.literal: The grand commander Yuan Xiuyi halted his army at Longkou and for a long time did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The grand commander Yuan Xiuyi halted at Longkou and for a long time would not advance.

sentences.zh: 念生復反，執士和送胡琛，於道殺之。

translations.literal: Niansheng rebelled again, seized Shihe and sent him to Hu Chen, who killed him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Niansheng rebelled again, seized Shihe and sent him to Hu Chen, who killed him on the road.

sentences.zh: 久之，伯度為-{万俟}-丑奴所殺，賊勢益盛，寶寅不能制。

translations.literal: After some time Bodu was killed by Moqi Chounu; the rebels grew stronger still, and Baoyin could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Bodu was killed by Moqi Chounu; the rebels grew stronger still, and Baoyin could not control them.

sentences.zh: 胡琛與莫折念生交通，事破六韓拔陵浸慢，拔陵遣其臣費律至高平，誘琛，斬之，丑奴盡並其眾。

translations.literal: Hu Chen had dealings with Moqi Niansheng; when the affair was exposed, Liu Han Baleng treated him with growing contempt. Baleng sent his minister Fei Lü to Gaoping to entice Chen and beheaded him; Chounu absorbed all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Chen had dealings with Moqi Niansheng; when this was exposed, Liu Han Baleng treated him with growing contempt, sent his minister Fei Lü to Gaoping to lure Chen out and beheaded him, and Chounu absorbed all his followers.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，庚辰，大赦。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on gengchen, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the eleventh month, on gengchen, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 丁貴嬪卒，太子水漿不入口，上使謂之曰；

translations.literal: When the Honored Consort Ding died, the crown prince would take no food or drink; the emperor sent someone to say to him:
translations.idiomatic: When the Honored Consort Ding died, the crown prince refused all food and drink; the emperor sent someone to tell him:

sentences.zh: 「毀不滅性，況我在邪！

translations.literal: "Grief must not destroy one's nature—how much more so when I am still alive!"
translations.idiomatic: "Grief must not destroy your nature—how much more so when I am still alive!"

sentences.zh: 」乃進粥數合。

translations.literal: He then took several bowls of gruel.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he take several bowls of gruel.

sentences.zh: 太子體素肥壯，腰帶十圍，至是減削過半。

translations.literal: The crown prince's body had always been stout and strong, his belt ten spans around; by this time he had wasted away by more than half.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had always been stout, his belt ten spans around; by now he had wasted away by more than half.

sentences.zh: 夏侯但等軍入魏境，所向皆下。

translations.literal: The armies of Xiahou Dan and others entered Wei territory and wherever they went, places submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Xiahou Dan and others entered Wei territory and wherever they went, places fell to them.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，魏揚州刺史李憲以壽陽降，宣猛將軍陳慶之入據其城，凡降城五十二，獲男女七萬五千口。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Li Xian, governor of Yang Province in Wei, surrendered Shouyang; the Fierce General Chen Qingzhi entered and held the city. In all, fifty-two cities surrendered, and seventy-five thousand men and women were taken.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Li Xian, governor of Yang Province in Wei, surrendered Shouyang; the Fierce General Chen Qingzhi entered and held the city. Fifty-two cities surrendered in all, yielding seventy-five thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，縱李憲還魏，復以壽陽為豫州，改合肥為南豫州，以夏侯但為豫、南豫二州刺史。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Li Xian was released to return to Wei; Shouyang was again made Yu Province, Hefei was changed to Southern Yu Province, and Xiahou Dan was made governor of both Yu and Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Li Xian was released to return to Wei; Shouyang was restored as Yu Province, Hefei was made Southern Yu Province, and Xiahou Dan was appointed governor of both.

sentences.zh: 壽陽久罹兵革，民眾流散，但輕荊薄賦，務農省役，頃之，民戶充復。

translations.literal: Shouyang had long suffered from warfare and the people had scattered; Dan lightened punishments and reduced levies, devoted effort to farming and curtailed corvée, and before long households were restored in full.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyang had long suffered warfare and its people had scattered; Dan lightened punishments, reduced levies, promoted farming, and curtailed corvée, and before long the population was restored.

sentences.zh: 杜洛周圍范陽，戊戌，民執魏幽州刺史王延年、行台常景送洛周，開門納之。

translations.literal: Du Luozhou besieged Fanyang; on wuxu the people seized Wang Yannian, governor of You Province in Wei, and the forward-army commander Chang Jing, handed them to Luozhou, and opened the gates to admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Luozhou besieged Fanyang; on wuxu the townspeople seized the Wei governor Wang Yannian and the forward-army commander Chang Jing, handed them to Luozhou, and opened the gates to him.

sentences.zh: 魏齊州平原民劉樹等反，攻陷郡縣，頻敗州軍。

translations.literal: Liu Shu and others among the people of Pingyuan in Qi Province of Wei rebelled, stormed commanderies and counties, and repeatedly defeated the provincial army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shu and others among the people of Pingyuan in Qi Province rebelled, stormed commanderies and counties, and repeatedly defeated the provincial army.

sentences.zh: 刺史元欣以平原房士達為將，討平之。

translations.literal: The governor Yuan Xin made Fang Shida of Pingyuan his general and suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: The governor Yuan Xin made Fang Shida of Pingyuan his general and put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 曹義宗據穰城以逼新野，魏遣都督魏承祖及尚書左丞、南道行台辛纂救之。

translations.literal: Cao Yizong held Rangcheng to press on Xinye; Wei sent the commander Wei Chengzu and the Left Director of the Masters of Writing and southern-route forward-army commander Xin Zuan to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yizong held Rangcheng to threaten Xinye; Wei sent the commander Wei Chengzu and the Left Director of the Masters of Writing and southern-route forward-army commander Xin Zuan to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 義宗戰不利，不敢進。

translations.literal: Yizong fought without success and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong fought without success and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 纂，雄之從父兄也。

translations.literal: Zuan was a cousin on his father's side of Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan was a paternal cousin of Xin Xiong.

sentences.zh: 魏盜賊日滋，征討不息，國用耗竭，預徽六年租調，猶不足，乃罷百官所給酒肉，又稅入得人一錢，及邸店皆有稅，百姓嗟怨。

translations.literal: Bandits and rebels in Wei grew daily; punitive campaigns never ceased; state revenues were exhausted. Even after levying six years' rent and corvée in advance, funds were still insufficient. Wine and meat rations for officials were cut off, a tax of one cash per person was imposed on entry, and inns and shops were all taxed—the people groaned in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry in Wei grew daily, punitive campaigns never ceased, and state revenues were exhausted. Even after levying six years' rent and corvée in advance, funds still fell short; officials' wine and meat rations were cut off, a head tax of one cash was imposed, inns and shops were taxed, and the people groaned in resentment.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎中辛雄上疏，以為：「夷夏之民相聚為亂，豈有餘憾哉！

translations.literal: Xin Xiong, a director in the Ministry of the Civil Service, submitted a memorial arguing: "When barbarian and Chinese folk gather to rebel, do they harbor leftover grievances?"
translations.idiomatic: Xin Xiong, a director in the Ministry of the Civil Service, submitted a memorial arguing, "When barbarian and Chinese subjects gather in revolt, is it because they still nurse old grievances?"

sentences.zh: 正以守令不得其人，百姓不堪其命故也。

translations.literal: "It is simply that the prefects and magistrates are not the right men, and the people cannot bear their rule."
translations.idiomatic: "It is because the prefects and magistrates are not the right men and the people cannot bear their rule."

sentences.zh: 宜及此時早加慰撫。

translations.literal: "At this time one should promptly offer comfort and reassurance."
translations.idiomatic: "At this time the court should promptly offer comfort and reassurance."

sentences.zh: 但郡縣選舉，由來共輕，貴游俊才，莫肯居此。

translations.literal: "Yet selection for commandery and county posts has always been held in low esteem, and no noble scions or outstanding talents are willing to take such offices."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet county and commandery posts have always been held in low esteem, and no noble scions or outstanding talents are willing to take them."

sentences.zh: 宜改其弊，分郡縣為三等，清官選補之法，妙盡才望，如不可並，後地先才，不得拘以停年。

translations.literal: "This abuse should be reformed: divide commanderies and counties into three grades and devise methods for selecting and filling pure offices that weigh talent and reputation to the utmost; when the two cannot be had together, let talent precede seniority and do not bind appointments to years of service."
translations.idiomatic: "This abuse should be reformed: divide commanderies and counties into three grades and select officials for pure offices by weighing talent and reputation to the utmost; when both cannot be had, let talent precede seniority and do not bind appointments to years of service."

sentences.zh: 三載黜陟，有稱職者，補在京名官；

translations.literal: "After three years of promotion and demotion, those who prove competent should be transferred to famous offices in the capital;"
translations.idiomatic: "After three years of review, those who prove competent should be transferred to prestigious offices in the capital;"

sentences.zh: 如不歷守令，不得為內職。

translations.literal: "those who have not served as prefect or magistrate may not hold inner-court posts."
translations.idiomatic: "those who have not served as prefect or magistrate may not hold inner-court posts."

sentences.zh: 則人思自勉，杜屈可申，強暴自息矣。

translations.literal: "Then men will strive to improve themselves, suppressed grievances can be voiced, and violence will cease of itself."
translations.idiomatic: "Then men will strive to improve themselves, suppressed grievances can be heard, and violence will cease of itself."

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: His advice was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝七大通元年（

translations.literal: The first year of Datong of Emperor Wu of the High Ancestor (
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong of Emperor Wu of the High Ancestor (

sentences.zh: 丁未，公元五二七年）

translations.literal: dingwei, A.D. 527)
translations.idiomatic: the year dingwei, A.D. 527)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙丑，以尚書左僕射徐逸為僕射。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yichou, Xu Yi, Vice Director of the Left among the Masters of Writing, was made Director.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on yichou, Xu Yi, Vice Director of the Left among the Masters of Writing, was made Director.

sentences.zh: 辛未，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，魏以司空皇甫度為司徒，儀同三司，蕭寶寅為司空。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Wei made the Minister of Works Huangfu Du Minister over the Masses with the rank of peer of the Three Excellencies, and Xiao Baoyin Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Wei made the Minister of Works Huangfu Du Minister over the Masses with the rank of peer of the Three Excellencies and appointed Xiao Baoyin Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 魏分定、相二州四郡置殷州，以北道行台博陵崔楷為刺史。

translations.literal: Wei carved out four commanderies from Ding and Xiang Provinces to establish Yin Province and appointed Cui Kai of Boling, commander of the northern-route forward army, as its governor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei carved out four commanderies from Ding and Xiang Provinces to establish Yin Province and appointed Cui Kai of Boling, commander of the northern-route forward army, as its governor.

sentences.zh: 楷表稱：「州今新立，尺刃斗糧，皆所未有，乞資以兵糧。

translations.literal: Kai submitted a memorial stating: "The province has only just been established; not even a foot of blade or a peck of grain is on hand—I beg supplies of military provisions."
translations.idiomatic: Kai memorialized: "The province has only just been established; we lack even weapons and grain—I beg military provisions."

sentences.zh: 」詔付外量聞，竟無所給。

translations.literal: An edict referred the matter to the outer offices for assessment, but in the end nothing was supplied.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the outer offices for assessment, but in the end nothing was supplied.

sentences.zh: 或勸楷留家，單騎之官，楷曰：「吾聞食人之祿者憂人之憂，若吾獨往，則將士誰肯固志哉！

translations.literal: Some urged Kai to leave his family behind and go to his post alone on horseback. Kai said, "I have heard that one who eats another's salary must share his lord's cares—if I go alone, who among the officers and men will hold firm in resolve?"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Kai to leave his family and ride alone to his post. Kai said, "One who eats another's salary must share his lord's cares—if I go alone, who among the officers and men will hold firm?"

sentences.zh: 」遂舉家之官。

translations.literal: He then took his whole household to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He then took his whole household with him to his post.

sentences.zh: 葛榮逼州城，或勸減弱小以避之，楷遣幼子及一女夜出；

translations.literal: Ge Rong pressed the provincial city; some urged sending away the weak to escape harm, and Kai sent his youngest son and one daughter out by night;
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong pressed the city, some urged sending away the weak; Kai sent his youngest son and one daughter out by night;

sentences.zh: 既而悔之，曰：「人謂吾心不固，虧忠而全愛也。

translations.literal: but then regretted it and said, "People will say my heart is not steadfast—that I sacrificed loyalty to preserve affection."
translations.idiomatic: but then regretted it and said, "People will say my heart is not steadfast—that I sacrificed loyalty to preserve my family."

sentences.zh: 」遂命追還。

translations.literal: He then ordered them brought back.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered them brought back.

sentences.zh: 賊至，強弱相懸，又無守禦之具；

translations.literal: When the rebels arrived, strength and weakness were utterly mismatched and there were no means of defense;
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived, the odds were hopeless and there were no means of defense;

sentences.zh: 楷撫勉將士以拒之，莫不爭奮，皆曰：「崔公尚不惜百口，吾屬何愛一身！

translations.literal: Kai comforted and exhorted the officers and men to resist; none failed to strive with ardor, all saying, "Lord Cui does not spare a hundred mouths—why should we cherish a single body!"
translations.idiomatic: Kai comforted and exhorted the officers and men to resist; all strove with ardor, saying, "Lord Cui does not spare a hundred lives—why should we cherish a single body!"

sentences.zh: 」連戰不息，死者相枕，終無叛志。

translations.literal: They fought without pause; the dead lay pillow to pillow, yet in the end none wavered in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: They fought without pause; the dead lay piled one upon another, yet none wavered in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 辛未，城陷，楷執節不屈，榮殺之，遂圍冀州。

translations.literal: On xinwei the city fell; Kai grasped his staff of office and would not submit, and Rong killed him, then besieged Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the city fell; Kai grasped his staff of office and would not submit, and Rong killed him, then besieged Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 魏蕭寶寅出兵累年，將士疲弊。

translations.literal: Xiao Baoyin of Wei had campaigned for many years, and officers and men were worn out.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin of Wei had campaigned for many years until his officers and men were worn out.

sentences.zh: 秦賊擊之，寶寅大敗於涇州，收散兵萬餘人，屯逍遙園，東秦州刺史潘義淵以汧城降賊。

translations.literal: The Qin rebels struck him; Baoyin suffered a great defeat at Jing Province, gathered more than ten thousand scattered troops, and encamped at Xiaoyaoyuan; Pan Yiyuan, governor of Eastern Qin Province, surrendered Qian city to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin rebels struck him; Baoyin suffered a crushing defeat at Jing Province, gathered more than ten thousand scattered troops, and encamped at Xiaoyaoyuan; Pan Yiyuan, governor of Eastern Qin Province, surrendered Qian city to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 莫折念生進逼岐州，城人執刺史魏蘭根應之。

translations.literal: Moqi Niansheng advanced to press Qi Province; the townspeople seized the governor Wei Lan'gen and joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi Niansheng advanced on Qi Province; the townspeople seized the governor Wei Lan'gen and joined him.

sentences.zh: 豳州刺史畢祖暉戰沒，行台辛深棄城走，北海王顥軍亦敗。

translations.literal: Bi Zuhui, governor of Bin Province, was killed in battle; the forward-army commander Xin Shen abandoned his city and fled; the army of the Prince of Beihai Hao was also defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zuhui, governor of Bin Province, fell in battle; the forward-army commander Xin Shen abandoned his city and fled; the army of the Prince of Beihai Yuan Hao was also defeated.

sentences.zh: 賊帥胡引祖據北華州，叱干麒麟據豳州以應天生，關中大擾。

translations.literal: The rebel leader Hu Yinzu held Northern Hua Province and Chigan Qilin held Bin Province in response to Tiansheng; the Guanzhong region was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Hu Yinzu held Northern Hua Province and Chigan Qilin held Bin Province in support of Moqi Tiansheng; the Guanzhong region was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史楊椿募兵得七千餘人，帥以拒守，詔加椿侍中兼尚書右僕射，為行台，節度關西諸將。

translations.literal: Yang Chun, governor of Yong Province, recruited more than seven thousand troops and led them to hold the line; an edict added Chun as Palace Attendant and concurrently Vice Director of the Right among the Masters of Writing, made him forward-army commander, and put the generals of the western passes under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun, governor of Yong Province, recruited more than seven thousand troops and led them to hold the line; an edict made him Palace Attendant and concurrently Vice Director of the Right among the Masters of Writing, forward-army commander, and commander of the generals of the western passes.

sentences.zh: 北地功曹毛鴻賓引賊抄掠渭北，雍州錄事參軍楊侃將兵三千掩擊之；

translations.literal: Mao Hongbin, a merit officer of Beidi, led rebels in raiding north of the Wei; Yang Kan, a recording secretary of Yong Province, led three thousand troops in a surprise attack on him;
translations.idiomatic: Mao Hongbin, a merit officer of Beidi, led rebels in raiding north of the Wei; Yang Kan of the Yang clan, a recording secretary of Yong Province, led three thousand troops in a surprise attack;

sentences.zh: 鴻賓懼，請討賊自效，遂擒送宿勤烏過仁。

translations.literal: Hongbin was afraid, asked to attack the rebels to prove his merit, and captured and sent Suqin Wuguoren.
translations.idiomatic: Hongbin was afraid, offered to attack the rebels to prove his loyalty, and captured and delivered Suqin Wuguoren.

sentences.zh: 烏過仁者，明達之兄子也。

translations.literal: Wuguoren was a nephew of Mingda on his elder brother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Wuguoren was a nephew of Suqin Mingda.

sentences.zh: 莫折天生乘勝寇雍州，蕭寶寅部將羊侃隱身塹中射之，應弦而斃，其眾遂潰。

translations.literal: Moqi Tiansheng followed up his victory to raid Yong Province; Yang Kan, a subordinate of Xiao Baoyin from the Yang clan, hid in the trench and shot him—he fell at the twang of the bowstring and his host scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi Tiansheng followed up his victory to raid Yong Province; Yang Kan, a subordinate of Xiao Baoyin from the Yang clan, hid in the trench and shot him—he fell at the twang of the bowstring and his host scattered.

sentences.zh: 侃，祉之子也。

translations.literal: Kan was the son of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: This Yang Kan was the son of Yang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 魏右民郎陽平路思令上疏，以為：「師出有功，在於將帥，得其人則六合唾掌可清，失其人則三河方為戰地。

translations.literal: Lu Siling of Yangping, a director in the Right Bureau of the People in Wei, submitted a memorial arguing: "Success in sending armies abroad lies in the commanders—with the right men the realm can be cleared as easily as spitting into one's palm; with the wrong men even the Three Rivers become a battlefield."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Siling of Yangping, a director in the Right Bureau of the People in Wei, submitted a memorial arguing, "Success in sending armies abroad lies in the commanders—with the right men the realm can be cleared as easily as spitting into one's palm; with the wrong men even the Three Rivers become a battlefield."

sentences.zh: 竊以比年將帥多寵貴子孫，銜杯躍馬，志逸氣浮，軒眉攘腕，以攻戰自許；

translations.literal: "I observe that in recent years most commanders are pampered scions of the noble houses—cup in hand, leaping on horseback, minds adrift and spirits buoyant, brows raised and sleeves rolled, boasting of prowess in attack and battle;"
translations.idiomatic: "In recent years most commanders are pampered noble scions—cup in hand, leaping on horseback, minds adrift and spirits buoyant, boasting of prowess in battle;"

sentences.zh: 及臨大敵，憂怖交懷，雄圖銳氣，一朝頓盡。

translations.literal: "yet when they face a great enemy, fear and dread fill their hearts together, and their bold designs and sharp ardor vanish in a single morning."
translations.idiomatic: "yet when they face a great enemy, fear fills their hearts and their bold designs vanish in a single morning."

sentences.zh: 乃令羸弱在前以當寇，強壯居後以衛身，兼復器械不精，進止無節，以當負險之眾，敵數戰之虜，欲其不敗，豈可得哉！

translations.literal: "They then place the weak and sickly in front to meet the foe and keep the strong in the rear to guard themselves; moreover their weapons are not well made and their advances and halts lack discipline—pitched against foes holding difficult ground and veterans of many battles, how can they hope not to be defeated!"
translations.idiomatic: "They place the weak in front to meet the foe and keep the strong in the rear to guard themselves; their weapons are poor and their advances and halts lack discipline—pitched against foes holding difficult ground and veterans of many battles, how can they hope not to be defeated!"

sentences.zh: 是以兵知必敗，始集而先逃；

translations.literal: "Thus the soldiers know defeat is certain and flee before the battle is joined;"
translations.idiomatic: "Thus the soldiers know defeat is certain and flee before the battle is joined;"

sentences.zh: 將帥畏敵，遷延而不進。

translations.literal: "the commanders fear the enemy and delay without advancing."
translations.idiomatic: "the commanders fear the enemy and delay without advancing."

sentences.zh: 國家謂官爵未滿，屢加寵命；

translations.literal: "The state thinks their offices and titles are not yet full enough and repeatedly adds favor and appointments;"
translations.idiomatic: "The state thinks their offices and titles are not yet high enough and repeatedly adds honors;"

sentences.zh: 復疑賞賚之輕，日散金帛。

translations.literal: "then suspects that rewards are too slight and daily scatters gold and silk."
translations.idiomatic: "then suspects rewards are too slight and daily scatters gold and silk."

sentences.zh: 帑藏空竭，民財殫盡，遂使賊徒益甚，生民凋弊，凡以此也。

translations.literal: "The treasury is emptied, the people's wealth exhausted—thus the rebels grow worse and the common folk are ruined; all of this stems from these causes."
translations.idiomatic: "The treasury is emptied, the people's wealth exhausted—the rebels grow worse and the common folk are ruined; all of this stems from these causes."

sentences.zh: 夫德可感義夫，恩可勸死士。

translations.literal: "Virtue can move men of principle; grace can stir men willing to die."
translations.idiomatic: "Virtue can move men of principle; grace can stir men willing to die."

sentences.zh: 今若黜陟幽明，賞罰善惡，簡練士卒，繕修器械，先遣辯士曉以禍福，如其不悛，以順討逆。

translations.literal: "If now one promotes and demotes the worthy and unworthy, rewards good and punishes evil, drills the soldiers, repairs weapons, first sends eloquent envoys to explain fortune and disaster, and if they do not repent, uses the righteous to chastise the rebellious—"
translations.idiomatic: "If the court now promotes and demotes the worthy and unworthy, rewards good and punishes evil, drills the soldiers, repairs weapons, first sends eloquent envoys to explain fortune and disaster, and if they do not repent, uses the righteous to chastise the rebellious—"

sentences.zh: 如此，則何異厲蕭斧而伐朝菌，鼓洪爐而燎毛髮哉！

translations.literal: "in this way, what difference would there be from whetting an axe to fell a morning mushroom, or stoking a great furnace to singe a hair!"
translations.idiomatic: "what difference would there be from whetting an axe to fell a morning mushroom, or stoking a great furnace to singe a hair!"

sentences.zh: 」弗聽。

translations.literal: His advice was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 戊子，魏以皇甫度為太尉。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Wei appointed Huangfu Du Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Wei appointed Huangfu Du Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 己丑，魏主以四方未平，詔內外戒嚴，將親出討，竟亦不行。

translations.literal: On jichou, because the four quarters were not yet pacified, the Wei sovereign issued an edict placing the realm on alert within and without and announcing that he would personally campaign; in the end this too was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, because the four quarters were not yet pacified, the Wei sovereign placed the realm on alert within and without and announced a personal campaign; in the end this too was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 譙州刺史湛僧智圍魏東豫州，將軍彭群、王辯圍琅邪，魏敕青、南青二州救琅邪。

translations.literal: Zhan Sengzhi, governor of Qiao Province, besieged Eastern Yu Province in Wei; the generals Peng Qun and Wang Bian besieged Langye; Wei ordered Qing and Southern Qing Provinces to rescue Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Sengzhi, governor of Qiao Province, besieged Eastern Yu Province in Wei; the generals Peng Qun and Wang Bian besieged Langye; Wei ordered Qing and Southern Qing Provinces to relieve Langye.

sentences.zh: 司州刺史夏侯夔帥壯武將軍裴之禮等出義陽道，攻魏平靜、穆陵、陰山三關，皆克之。

translations.literal: Xiahou Kui, governor of Si Province, led the Robust Martial General Pei Zhili and others out by the Yiyang route, attacked the three passes of Pingjing, Muling, and Yinshan in Wei, and took them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Kui, governor of Si Province, led the Robust Martial General Pei Zhili and others out by the Yiyang route, attacked the three Wei passes of Pingjing, Muling, and Yinshan, and took them all.

sentences.zh: 夔，但之弟；

translations.literal: Kui was the younger brother of Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was the younger brother of Xiahou Dan.

sentences.zh: 之禮，邃之子也。

translations.literal: Zhili was the son of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili was the son of Pei Sui.

sentences.zh: 魏東清河郡山賊群起，詔以齊州長史房景伯為東清河太守。

translations.literal: Mountain bandits rose in groups in Eastern Qinghe commandery of Wei; an edict appointed Fang Jingbo, chief clerk of Qi Province, governor of Eastern Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain bandits rose in Eastern Qinghe commandery in Wei; an edict appointed Fang Jingbo, chief clerk of Qi Province, governor of Eastern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 郡民劉簡虎嘗無禮於景伯，舉家亡去。

translations.literal: Liu Jianhu, a man of the commandery, had once been disrespectful to Jingbo and fled with his whole household.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianhu, a man of the commandery, had once been disrespectful to Jingbo and fled with his whole household.

sentences.zh: 景伯窮捕，擒之，署其子為西曹掾，令諭山賊。

translations.literal: Jingbo hunted him relentlessly, captured him, appointed his son a Western Bureau aide, and ordered him to persuade the mountain bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo hunted him down, captured him, appointed his son a Western Bureau aide, and ordered him to persuade the mountain bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊以景伯不念舊惡，皆相帥出降。

translations.literal: Because the bandits saw that Jingbo did not bear old grudges, they all led one another out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Jingbo did not bear old grudges, the bandits all led one another out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 景伯母崔氏，通經，有明識。

translations.literal: Jingbo's mother, the Lady Cui, was versed in the classics and had clear judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo's mother, Lady Cui, was versed in the classics and had clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 貝丘婦人列其子不孝，景伯以白其母，母曰：「吾聞聞名不如見面，山民未知禮義，何足深責！

translations.literal: A woman of Beiqiu accused her son of unfilial conduct; Jingbo reported this to his mother, who said, "I have heard that hearing a name is not like meeting the face—the mountain folk do not yet know ritual and righteousness; why blame them deeply!"
translations.idiomatic: A woman of Beiqiu accused her son of unfilial conduct; Jingbo reported this to his mother, who said, "Hearing a name is not like meeting the face—the mountain folk do not yet know ritual and righteousness; why blame them deeply!"

sentences.zh: 」乃召其母，與之對榻共食，使其子侍立堂下，觀景伯供食。

translations.literal: She then summoned the mother, shared a couch and ate with her, and had the son wait standing below the hall to watch Jingbo serve food.
translations.idiomatic: She summoned the mother, shared a couch and ate with her, and had the son wait below the hall to watch Jingbo serve food.

sentences.zh: 未旬日，悔過求還；

translations.literal: In less than ten days he repented and asked to return;
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he repented and asked to return;

sentences.zh: 崔氏曰：「此雖面慚，其心未也，且置之。

translations.literal: the Lady Cui said, "Though he is ashamed in face, his heart is not yet so—let it be for now."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui said, "Though he is ashamed in face, his heart is not yet changed—let it be for now."

sentences.zh: 」凡二十餘日，其子叩頭流血，母涕泣乞還，然後聽之，卒以孝聞。

translations.literal: After more than twenty days the son knocked his head until it bled and the mother wept and begged for his return; only then did she consent, and in the end he became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty days the son knocked his head until it bled and the mother wept and begged for his return; only then did she consent, and in the end he became known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 景伯，法壽之族子也。

translations.literal: Jingbo was a clansman of Fashou on his father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo was a clansman of Fang Fashou.

sentences.zh: 二月，秦賊據魏潼關。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Qin rebels seized Tong Pass in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the Qin rebels seized Tong Pass in Wei.

sentences.zh: 庚申，魏東郡民趙顯德反，殺太守裴煙，自號都督。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Zhao Xiande of the people of Dong commandery in Wei rebelled, killed the governor Pei Yan, and styled himself commander.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Zhao Xiande of Dong commandery in Wei rebelled, killed the governor Pei Yan, and styled himself commander.

sentences.zh: 將軍成景俊攻魏彭城，魏以前荊州刺史崔孝芬為徐州行台以御之。

translations.literal: The general Cheng Jingjun attacked Pengcheng in Wei; Wei appointed the former governor of Jing Province Cui Xiaofen forward-army commander of Xu Province to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: The general Cheng Jingjun attacked Pengcheng in Wei; Wei appointed the former governor of Jing Province Cui Xiaofen forward-army commander of Xu Province to resist him.

sentences.zh: 先是，孝芬坐元義黨與盧同等俱除名，及將赴徐州，入辭太后，太后謂孝芬曰：「我與卿姻戚，奈何內頭元義車中，稱『此老嫗會須去之！

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiaofen had been implicated as a partisan of Yuan Yi along with Lu Tong and others and stripped of rank; when he was about to go to Xu Province he entered to take leave of the empress dowager. The empress dowager said to Xiaofen, "You and I are kin by marriage—why, inside Yuan Yi's carriage, did you say, 'This old woman will have to go!'"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiaofen had been implicated as a partisan of Yuan Yi along with Lu Tong and others and stripped of rank; when he was about to depart for Xu Province he took leave of the empress dowager, who said to him, "You and I are kin by marriage—why, inside Yuan Yi's carriage, did you say, 'This old woman will have to go!'"

sentences.zh: 』」孝芬曰：「臣蒙國厚恩，實無斯語。

translations.literal: Xiaofen said, "Your servant has received thick favor from the state and in truth never spoke such words."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaofen said, "I have received thick favor from the state and in truth never spoke such words."

sentences.zh: 假令有之，誰能得聞！

translations.literal: "Even if I had, who could have heard it!"
translations.idiomatic: "Even if I had, who could have heard it!"

sentences.zh: 若有聞者，此於元義親密過臣遠矣。

translations.literal: "If anyone heard it, that person would be far more intimate with Yuan Yi than I."
translations.idiomatic: "If anyone heard it, that person would be far more intimate with Yuan Yi than I."

sentences.zh: 」太后意解，悵然有愧色。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's mind was eased, and she looked regretful and ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's anger eased, and she looked regretful and ashamed.

sentences.zh: 景俊欲堰泗水以灌彭城，孝芬與都督李叔仁等擊之，景俊遁還。

translations.literal: Jingjun wished to dam the Si River to inundate Pengcheng; Xiaofen and the commander Li Shuren and others struck him, and Jingjun fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjun wished to dam the Si River to inundate Pengcheng; Xiaofen and the commander Li Shuren and others struck him, and Jingjun fled back.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲子，魏主詔將西討，中外戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jiazi, the Wei sovereign issued an edict announcing a western campaign; within and without, the realm was placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiazi, the Wei sovereign announced a western campaign and placed the realm on alert within and without.

sentences.zh: 會秦賊西走，復得潼關，戊辰，詔回駕北討。

translations.literal: When the Qin rebels fled west, Tong Pass was recovered; on wuchen an edict ordered the imperial carriage to turn back for a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qin rebels fled west, Tong Pass was recovered; on wuchen an edict ordered the imperial carriage to turn back for a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 其實皆不行。

translations.literal: In fact neither was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In fact neither campaign was carried out.

sentences.zh: 葛榮久圍信都，魏以金紫光祿大夫源子邕為北討大都督以救之。

translations.literal: Ge Rong had long besieged Xindu; Wei appointed Yuan Ziyong, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, grand commander of the northern punitive campaign to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong had long besieged Xindu; Wei appointed Yuan Ziyong, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, grand commander of the northern punitive campaign to rescue it.

sentences.zh: 初，上作同泰寺，又開大通門以對之，取其反語相協。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor built Tongtai Temple and also opened the Great Passage Gate to face it, taking the reverse reading of the names as a harmonious omen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the emperor built Tongtai Temple and also opened the Great Passage Gate to face it, taking the reverse reading of the names as a harmonious omen.

sentences.zh: 上晨夕幸寺，皆出入是門。

translations.literal: Morning and evening the emperor visited the temple, always entering and leaving by this gate.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening the emperor visited the temple, always entering and leaving by this gate.

sentences.zh: 辛未，上幸寺捨身；

translations.literal: On xinwei the emperor visited the temple and surrendered his person;
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the emperor visited the temple and surrendered his person to the monastery;

sentences.zh: 甲戌，還宮，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: on jiaxu he returned to the palace, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: on jiaxu he returned to the palace, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 魏齊州廣川民劉鈞聚眾反，自署大行台；

translations.literal: Liu Jun of the people of Guangchuan in Qi Province of Wei gathered a host and rebelled, styling himself commander of the great forward army;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun of Guangchuan in Qi Province gathered followers and rebelled, styling himself commander of the great forward army;

sentences.zh: 清河民房須自署大都督，屯據昌國城。

translations.literal: Fang Xu of Qinghe commandery styled himself grand commander and encamped at Changguo city.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xu of Qinghe styled himself grand commander and held Changguo city.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，魏將元斌之討東郡，斬趙顯德。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Wei general Yuan Binzhi attacked Dong commandery and beheaded Zhao Xiande.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, the Wei general Yuan Binzhi attacked Dong commandery and beheaded Zhao Xiande.

sentences.zh: 己酉，柔然頭兵可汗遣使入貢於魏，且請討群賊。

translations.literal: On jiyou, the Toubing Khan of Rouran sent envoys to offer tribute to Wei and also asked to campaign against the rebel bands.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, the Toubing Khan of Rouran sent envoys to offer tribute to Wei and also asked to campaign against the rebel bands.

sentences.zh: 魏人畏其反覆，詔以盛暑，且俟後敕。

translations.literal: The people of Wei feared their fickleness and issued an edict citing the height of summer and telling them to await further orders.
translations.idiomatic: Wei feared their fickleness and issued an edict citing the height of summer and telling them to await further orders.

sentences.zh: 魏蕭寶寅之敗也，有司處以死刑，詔免為庶人。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin of Wei was defeated, the authorities sentenced him to death, but an edict pardoned him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin of Wei was defeated, the authorities sentenced him to death, but an edict pardoned him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史楊椿有疾求解，復以寶寅為都督雍、涇等四州諸軍事、征西將軍、雍州刺史、開府儀同三司、西討大都督，自關以西皆受節度。

translations.literal: Yang Chun, governor of Yong Province, fell ill and asked to be relieved; Baoyin was again made commander of all armies of Yong, Jing, and four other provinces, General Who Campaigns West, governor of Yong Province, opener of a government office with the rank of peer of the Three Excellencies, and grand commander of the western punitive campaign—all west of the passes were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chun, governor of Yong Province, fell ill and asked to be relieved; Baoyin was again made commander of Yong, Jing, and four other provinces, General Who Campaigns West, governor of Yong Province, opener of a government office with the rank of peer of the Three Excellencies, and grand commander of the western punitive campaign—all west of the passes were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 椿還鄉里，其子昱將適洛陽，椿謂之曰：「當今雍州刺史亦無逾寶寅者，但其上佐，朝廷應遣心膂重人，何得任其牒用！

translations.literal: Chun returned to his home district; his son Yu was about to go to Luoyang. Chun said to him, "Among present governors of Yong Province none surpasses Baoyin, yet for his senior aides the court ought to send men of the utmost trust—how can he be allowed to appoint whom he lists!"
translations.idiomatic: Chun returned home; his son Yu was about to go to Luoyang. Chun told him, "Among present governors of Yong Province none surpasses Baoyin, yet for his senior aides the court ought to send men of the utmost trust—how can he be allowed to appoint whom he lists!"

sentences.zh: 此乃聖朝百慮之一失也。

translations.literal: "This is one lapse among the myriad concerns of the sacred court."
translations.idiomatic: "This is one lapse among the myriad concerns of the sacred court."

sentences.zh: 且寶寅不藉刺史為榮，吾觀其得州，喜悅特甚，至於賞罰雲為，不依常憲，恐有異心。

translations.literal: "Moreover Baoyin does not take glory from the governorship; I observe that when he obtained the province he was exceedingly joyful, and in meting out rewards and punishments he does not follow the usual statutes—I fear he harbors ulterior designs."
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover Baoyin does not take glory from the governorship alone; I observe that when he obtained the province he was exceedingly joyful, and in meting out rewards and punishments he does not follow the usual statutes—I fear he harbors ulterior designs."

sentences.zh: 汝今赴京師，當以吾此意啟二聖，並白宰輔，更遣長史、司馬、防城都督，欲安關中，正須三人耳。

translations.literal: "You are now going to the capital; you should report this thought of mine to the Two Sovereigns and inform the chief ministers as well, asking that a chief clerk, a marshal, and a garrison commander be sent anew—to secure Guanzhong, these three men are precisely what is needed."
translations.idiomatic: "You are now going to the capital; report this thought of mine to the Two Sovereigns and inform the chief ministers as well, asking that a chief clerk, a marshal, and a garrison commander be sent anew—to secure Guanzhong, these three men are precisely what is needed."

sentences.zh: 如其不遣，必成深憂。

translations.literal: "If they are not sent, deep worry is sure to follow."
translations.idiomatic: "If they are not sent, deep worry is sure to follow."

sentences.zh: 」昱面啟魏主及太后，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Yu reported this in person to the Wei sovereign and the empress dowager; neither would listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu reported this in person to the Wei sovereign and the empress dowager; neither would listen.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙寅，成景俊攻魏臨潼、竹邑，拔之。
