translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingyin, Cheng Jingjun attacked Lintong and Zhuyi in Wei and took them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingyin, Cheng Jingjun attacked Lintong and Zhuyi in Wei and took them.

sentences.zh: 東宮直閣蘭欽攻魏蕭城、厥固，拔之，欽斬魏將曹龍牙。

translations.literal: Lan Qin, an attendant at the Eastern Palace, attacked Xiaocheng and Juegu in Wei, took them, and Qin beheaded the Wei general Cao Longya.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Qin, an attendant at the Eastern Palace, attacked Xiaocheng and Juegu in Wei, took them, and beheaded the Wei general Cao Longya.

sentences.zh: 六月，魏都督李叔仁討劉鈞，平之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Wei commander Li Shuren attacked Liu Jun and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, the Wei commander Li Shuren attacked Liu Jun and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏陳郡民劉獲、鄭辯反於西華，改元天授，與湛僧智通謀，魏以行東豫州刺史譙國曹世表為東南道行台以討之，源子恭代世表為東豫州。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Liu Huo and Zheng Bian of Chen commandery in Wei rebelled at Xihua, changed the era name to Tianshou, and plotted with Zhan Sengzhi; Wei appointed Cao Shibiao of Qiaoguo, acting governor of Eastern Yu Province, forward-army commander of the southeastern route to suppress them, and Yuan Zigong replaced Shibiao in Eastern Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Liu Huo and Zheng Bian of Chen commandery rebelled at Xihua, proclaimed the era name Tianshou, and plotted with Zhan Sengzhi; Wei appointed Cao Shibiao of Qiaoguo, acting governor of Eastern Yu Province, forward-army commander of the southeastern route to suppress them, and Yuan Zigong replaced Shibiao in Eastern Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 諸將以賊眾強，官軍弱，且皆敗散之餘，不敢戰，欲保城自固。

translations.literal: The generals thought the rebels numerous and strong, the government troops few and weak, and all remnants of defeated and scattered forces—they dared not fight and wished only to hold the city and fortify themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The generals thought the rebels numerous and the government troops few and weak, all remnants of defeated forces—they dared not fight and wished only to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 世表方病背腫，輿出，呼統軍是雲寶謂曰：「湛僧智所以敢深入為寇者，以獲、辯皆州民之望，為之內應也。

translations.literal: Shibiao was just then ill with a swelling on his back; he was carried out in a litter and called the commander Shiyun Bao, saying, "The reason Zhan Sengzhi dares to raid deep inland is that Huo and Bian are both men in whom the people of the province place their hopes, serving as his allies within."
translations.idiomatic: Shibiao was ill with a swelling on his back; he was carried out in a litter and called the commander Shiyun Bao, saying, "Zhan Sengzhi dares raid deep inland because Huo and Bian are both men in whom the people of the province place their hopes, serving as his allies within."

sentences.zh: 向聞獲引兵欲迎僧智，去此八十里；

translations.literal: "I have just heard that Huo is leading troops to welcome Sengzhi, eighty li from here;"
translations.idiomatic: "I have just heard that Huo is leading troops to welcome Sengzhi, eighty li from here;"

sentences.zh: 今出其不意，一戰可破，獲破，則僧智自走矣。

translations.literal: "if we strike now by surprise, one battle can break them; once Huo is broken, Sengzhi will flee of himself."
translations.idiomatic: "if we strike now by surprise, one battle can break them; once Huo is broken, Sengzhi will flee of himself."

sentences.zh: 」乃選士馬付寶，暮出城，比曉而至，擊獲，大破之，窮討餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: He then selected troops and horses and gave them to Bao; they left the city at dusk, arrived by dawn, struck Huo, inflicted a great defeat, and pursued the remnant factions until all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He then selected troops and horses for Bao; they left the city at dusk, arrived by dawn, struck Huo, routed him, and pursued the remnant factions until all were pacified.

sentences.zh: 僧智聞之，遁還。

translations.literal: When Sengzhi heard of it he fled back.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengzhi heard of it he fled back.

sentences.zh: 鄭辯與子恭親舊，亡匿子恭所，世表集將吏面責子恭，收辯，斬之。

translations.literal: Zheng Bian was an old friend of Zigong and hid with him; Shibiao assembled the officers and rebuked Zigong to his face, seized Bian, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Bian was an old friend of Zigong and hid with him; Shibiao assembled the officers, rebuked Zigong to his face, seized Bian, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 魏相州刺史樂安王鑒與北道都督衍共救信都。

translations.literal: Yuan Jian, Prince of Le'an and governor of Xiang Province in Wei, and the northern-route commander Yan together went to rescue Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jian, Prince of Le'an and governor of Xiang Province in Wei, and the northern-route commander Pei Yan together went to rescue Xindu.

sentences.zh: 鑒幸魏多故，陰有異志，遂據鄴叛，降葛榮。

translations.literal: Jian rejoiced that Wei was beset by many troubles and secretly harbored ulterior designs; he then seized Ye in rebellion and surrendered to Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Jian rejoiced that Wei was beset by troubles and secretly harbored ulterior designs; he seized Ye in rebellion and surrendered to Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 己丑，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On jichou, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 初，侍御史遼東高道穆奉使相州，前刺史李世哲奢縱不法，道穆案之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gao Daomu of Liaodong, an attendant censor, was sent on mission to Xiang Province; the former governor Li Shizhe was extravagant, unrestrained, and lawless, and Daomu investigated him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gao Daomu of Liaodong, an attendant censor, was sent on mission to Xiang Province; the former governor Li Shizhe was extravagant, unrestrained, and lawless, and Daomu investigated him.

sentences.zh: 世哲弟神軌用事，道穆兄謙之家奴訴良，神軌收謙之系廷尉。

translations.literal: Shizhe's younger brother Shengui held power; a household slave of Daomu's elder brother Qianzhi sued for free status, and Shengui seized Qianzhi and imprisoned him in the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhe's younger brother Shengui held power; a household slave of Daomu's elder brother Qianzhi sued for free status, and Shengui seized Qianzhi and imprisoned him in the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 赦將出，神軌啟太后先賜謙之死，朝士哀之。

translations.literal: When an amnesty was about to be issued, Shengui memorialized the empress dowager to grant Qianzhi death beforehand; court gentlemen mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty was about to be issued, Shengui memorialized the empress dowager to have Qianzhi executed beforehand; court gentlemen mourned him.

sentences.zh: 彭群、王辯圍琅邪，自夏及秋，魏青州刺史彭城王劭遣司馬鹿悆、南青州刺史胡平遣長史劉仁之將兵擊群、辯，破之，群戰沒。

translations.literal: Peng Qun and Wang Bian besieged Langye from summer through autumn; Yuan Shao, Prince of Pengcheng and governor of Qing Province in Wei, sent the marshal Lu Yu, and Hu Ping, governor of Southern Qing Province, sent the chief clerk Liu Renzhi with troops to attack Qun and Bian, defeated them, and Qun was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Qun and Wang Bian besieged Langye from summer through autumn; Yuan Shao, Prince of Pengcheng and governor of Qing Province in Wei, sent the marshal Lu Yu, and Hu Ping, governor of Southern Qing Province, sent the chief clerk Liu Renzhi with troops to attack them, defeated them, and Qun fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 劭，勰之子也。

translations.literal: Shao was the son of Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was the son of Yuan Xie.

sentences.zh: 八月，魏遣都督源之邕，李神軌，裴衍攻鄴。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Wei sent the commanders Yuan Zhiyong, Li Shengui, and Pei Yan to attack Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Wei sent the commanders Yuan Zhiyong, Li Shengui, and Pei Yan to attack Ye.

sentences.zh: 子邕行及湯陰，安樂王鑒遣弟斌之夜襲子邕營，不克；

translations.literal: As Zhiyong marched and reached Tangyin, Jian, Prince of Le'an, sent his younger brother Bin to raid Zhiyong's camp by night, but did not succeed;
translations.idiomatic: As Zhiyong marched to Tangyin, Jian, Prince of Le'an, sent his younger brother Bin to raid Zhiyong's camp by night without success;

sentences.zh: 子邕乘勝進圍鄴城，丁未，拔之，斬鑒，傳首洛陽，改姓拓跋氏。

translations.literal: Zhiyong followed up his victory and advanced to besiege Ye; on dingwei he took it, beheaded Jian, sent his head to Luoyang, and changed his surname to the Tabgach clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyong followed up his victory and besieged Ye; on dingwei he took it, beheaded Jian, sent his head to Luoyang, and changed his surname to the imperial Tabgach clan name.

sentences.zh: 魏因遣子邕、裴衍討葛榮。

translations.literal: Wei then sent Zhiyong and Pei Yan to campaign against Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei then sent Zhiyong and Pei Yan to campaign against Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 九月，秦州城民杜粲殺莫折念生闔門皆盡，粲自行州事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Du Can of the townspeople of Qin Province killed Moqi Niansheng and wiped out his entire household; Can then administered the province on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Du Can of Qin Province killed Moqi Niansheng and wiped out his entire household, then administered the province on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 南秦州城民辛琛亦自行州事，遣使詣蕭寶寅請降。

translations.literal: Xin Chen of the townspeople of Southern Qin Province also administered the province on his own authority and sent envoys to Xiao Baoyin to ask to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Chen of Southern Qin Province also administered the province on his own authority and sent envoys to Xiao Baoyin to offer surrender.

sentences.zh: 魏復以寶寅為尚書令，還其舊封。

translations.literal: Wei again made Baoyin Director of the Masters of Writing and restored his former fief.
translations.idiomatic: Wei again made Baoyin Director of the Masters of Writing and restored his former fief.

sentences.zh: 譙州刺史湛僧智圍魏東豫州刺史元慶和於廣陵，魏將軍元顯伯救之，司州刺史夏侯夔自武陽引兵助僧智。

translations.literal: Zhan Sengzhi, governor of Qiao Province, besieged Yuan Qinghe, governor of Eastern Yu Province in Wei, at Guangling; the Wei general Yuan Xianbo went to rescue him, and Xiahou Kui, governor of Si Province, led troops from Wuyang to aid Sengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Sengzhi, governor of Qiao Province, besieged Yuan Qinghe, governor of Eastern Yu Province in Wei, at Guangling; the Wei general Yuan Xianbo went to rescue him, and Xiahou Kui, governor of Si Province, led troops from Wuyang to aid Sengzhi.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，夔至城下，慶和舉城降。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Kui reached the foot of the walls and Qinghe surrendered the whole city.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Kui reached the walls and Qinghe surrendered the whole city.

sentences.zh: 夔以讓僧智，僧智曰：「慶和欲降公，不欲降僧智，今往，必乖其意。

translations.literal: Kui wished to yield the honor to Sengzhi; Sengzhi said, "Qinghe wishes to surrender to Your Lordship, not to Sengzhi—if I go now, it will surely go against his intent."
translations.idiomatic: Kui wished to yield the honor to Sengzhi; Sengzhi said, "Qinghe wishes to surrender to you, not to me—if I go now, it will surely go against his intent."

sentences.zh: 且僧智所將應募烏合之人，不可御以法；

translations.literal: "Moreover the men I lead are recruited rabble and cannot be governed by strict law;"
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover the men I lead are recruited rabble and cannot be governed by strict law;"

sentences.zh: 公持軍素嚴，必無侵暴，受降納附，深得其宜。

translations.literal: "Your Lordship has always held the army strictly and will surely permit no pillage—receiving surrender and winning adherence, you are deeply suited to the task."
translations.idiomatic: "You have always held the army strictly and will surely permit no pillage—receiving surrender and winning adherence, you are deeply suited to the task."

sentences.zh: 」夔乃登城，拔魏幟，建梁幟；

translations.literal: Kui then mounted the walls, pulled down the Wei banners, and raised Liang banners;
translations.idiomatic: Kui then mounted the walls, pulled down the Wei banners, and raised Liang banners;

sentences.zh: 慶和束兵而出，吏民安堵，獲男女四萬餘口。

translations.literal: Qinghe bound up his weapons and came out; officials and people were settled in peace, and more than forty thousand men and women were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe bound up his weapons and came out; officials and people were settled in peace, and more than forty thousand men and women were taken.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：湛僧智可謂君子矣！

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: Zhan Sengzhi may be called a gentleman!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: Zhan Sengzhi may truly be called a gentleman!

sentences.zh: 忘其積時攻戰之勞，以授一朝新至之將，知己之短，不掩人之長，功成不取，以濟國事，忠且無私，可謂君子矣！

translations.literal: He forgot the toil of long campaigning and handed the credit to a general who had just arrived; he knew his own shortcomings and did not conceal another's strengths; when success was achieved he did not seize it but used it to advance the state's affairs—loyal and without selfishness, he may be called a gentleman!
translations.idiomatic: He forgot the toil of long campaigning and handed the credit to a newly arrived general; he knew his own shortcomings and did not conceal another's strengths; when success was achieved he did not seize it but used it to advance the state's affairs—loyal and without selfishness, he may truly be called a gentleman!

sentences.zh: 元顯伯宵遁，諸軍追之，斬獲萬計。

translations.literal: Yuan Xianbo fled by night; the armies pursued him and beheaded or captured tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xianbo fled by night; the armies pursued him and beheaded or captured tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 詔以僧智領東豫州刺史，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Sengzhi acting governor of Eastern Yu Province, stationed at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Sengzhi acting governor of Eastern Yu Province, stationed at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 夔引軍屯安陽，遣別將屠楚城，由是義陽北道遂與魏絕。

translations.literal: Kui led his army to encamp at Anyang, sent a detached general to storm Chucheng, and thereby the northern route of Yiyang was cut off from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Kui led his army to encamp at Anyang, sent a detached general to storm Chucheng, and thereby cut the northern route of Yiyang off from Wei.

sentences.zh: 領軍曹仲宗、東宮直閤陳慶之攻魏渦陽，詔尋陽太守韋放將兵會之。

translations.literal: The army commander Cao Zhongzong and Chen Qingzhi, an attendant of the Eastern Palace, attacked Woyang in Wei; an edict ordered Wei Fang, governor of Xunyang, to lead troops to join them.
translations.idiomatic: The army commander Cao Zhongzong and Chen Qingzhi, an attendant of the Eastern Palace, attacked Woyang in Wei; an edict ordered Wei Fang, governor of Xunyang, to lead troops to join them.

sentences.zh: 魏散騎常侍費穆引兵奄至，放營壘未立，麾下止有二百餘人，放免冑下馬，據胡床處分，士皆殊死戰，莫不一當百，魏兵遂退。

translations.literal: Fei Mu, Attendant at the Imperial Mount in Wei, led troops that arrived suddenly; Fang's camp was not yet established and he had only a little more than two hundred men under him. Fang removed his helmet, dismounted, sat on a folding chair to give orders, and the soldiers all fought as if ready to die, each matching a hundred; the Wei troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Mu, Attendant at the Imperial Mount in Wei, led troops that arrived suddenly; Fang's camp was not yet established and he had only a little more than two hundred men. Fang removed his helmet, dismounted, sat on a folding chair to give orders, and the soldiers fought as if ready to die, each matching a hundred; the Wei troops withdrew.

sentences.zh: 放，睿之子也。

translations.literal: Fang was the son of Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was the son of Wei Rui.

sentences.zh: 魏又遣將軍元昭等眾五萬救渦陽，前軍至駝澗，去渦陽四十里。

translations.literal: Wei again sent the general Yuan Zhao and others with fifty thousand men to rescue Woyang; the vanguard reached Tuojian, forty li from Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei again sent the general Yuan Zhao and others with fifty thousand men to rescue Woyang; the vanguard reached Tuojian, forty li from Woyang.

sentences.zh: 陳慶之欲逆戰，韋放以魏之前鋒必皆輕銳，不如勿擊，待其來至。

translations.literal: Chen Qingzhi wished to give battle; Wei Fang thought the Wei vanguard must all be light and elite troops and that it would be better not to strike but to wait until they arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingzhi wished to give battle; Wei Fang thought the Wei vanguard must all be light elite troops and that it would be better to wait until they arrived.

sentences.zh: 慶之曰；

translations.literal: Qingzhi said:
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said:

sentences.zh: 「魏兵遠來疲倦，去我既遠，必不見疑，及其未集，須挫其氣。

translations.literal: "The Wei troops have come from afar and are weary; they are already far from us and surely will not suspect us—before they gather we must break their spirit."
translations.idiomatic: "The Wei troops have come from afar and are weary; they are already far from us and will not suspect us—before they gather we must break their spirit."

sentences.zh: 諸君若疑，慶之請獨取之。

translations.literal: "If you gentlemen are in doubt, Qingzhi asks to take them alone."
translations.idiomatic: "If you gentlemen are in doubt, let Qingzhi take them alone."

sentences.zh: 」於是帥麾下二百騎進擊，破之，魏人驚駭。

translations.literal: He then led two hundred horsemen under his command in an attack, defeated them, and the Wei men were shocked and terrified.
translations.idiomatic: He then led two hundred horsemen in an attack, routed them, and the Wei troops were shocked and terrified.

sentences.zh: 慶之乃還，與諸將連營而進，背渦陽城與魏軍相持。

translations.literal: Qingzhi then returned, joined camps with the other generals, and advanced with his back to Woyang city in stalemate against the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi then returned, joined camps with the other generals, and advanced with his back to Woyang city in stalemate against the Wei army.

sentences.zh: 自春至冬，數十百戰，將士疲弊。

translations.literal: From spring through winter they fought scores and hundreds of battles; officers and men were worn out.
translations.idiomatic: From spring through winter they fought scores of battles; officers and men were worn out.

sentences.zh: 聞魏人欲築壘於軍後，曹仲宗等恐腹背受敵，議引軍還。

translations.literal: When they heard that the Wei men wished to build fortifications behind the army, Cao Zhongzong and others feared being attacked front and rear and discussed withdrawing the army.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard that the Wei men wished to build fortifications behind the army, Cao Zhongzong and others feared being attacked front and rear and discussed withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 慶之杖節軍門曰：「共來至此，涉歷一歲，糜費極多。

translations.literal: Qingzhi staff in hand at the army gate said, "We have all come here together and passed a full year, with vast expenditures."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi, staff in hand at the army gate, said, "We have all come here together and passed a full year at vast expense."

sentences.zh: 今諸君皆無鬥心，唯謀退縮，豈是欲立功名，直聚為抄暴耳！

translations.literal: "Now you gentlemen all lack fighting spirit and think only of retreat—do you wish to establish merit and fame, or have you simply gathered to plunder and ravage!"
translations.idiomatic: "Now you gentlemen all lack fighting spirit and think only of retreat—do you wish to establish merit and fame, or have you simply gathered to plunder!"

sentences.zh: 吾聞置兵死地，乃可求生；

translations.literal: "I have heard that when troops are placed in deadly ground, life may then be sought;"
translations.idiomatic: "I have heard that when troops are placed in deadly ground, life may then be sought;"

sentences.zh: 須虜大合，然後與戰。

translations.literal: "we must wait until the enemy gathers in full, and only then give battle."
translations.idiomatic: "we must wait until the enemy gathers in full, and only then give battle."

sentences.zh: 審欲班師，慶之別有密敕，今日犯者，當依敕行之！

translations.literal: "If you truly wish to withdraw the army, Qingzhi has a separate secret edict—whoever offends today shall be dealt with according to that edict!"
translations.idiomatic: "If you truly wish to withdraw, Qingzhi has a separate secret edict—whoever offends today shall be dealt with according to that edict!"

sentences.zh: 」仲宗等乃止。

translations.literal: Zhongzong and the others then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong and the others then stopped.

sentences.zh: 魏人作十三城，欲以控制梁軍。

translations.literal: The Wei men built thirteen cities to control the Liang army.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei men built thirteen fortified positions to control the Liang army.

sentences.zh: 慶之銜枚夜出，陷其四城，渦陽城主王緯乞降。

translations.literal: Qingzhi went out by night with gags in the soldiers' mouths, took four of the cities, and Wang Wei, lord of Woyang, begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi went out by night with gags in the soldiers' mouths, took four of the positions, and Wang Wei, lord of Woyang, begged to surrender.

sentences.zh: 韋放簡遣降者三十餘人分報魏諸營，陳慶之陳其俘馘，鼓噪隨之，魏九城皆潰，追擊之，俘斬略盡，屍咽渦水，所降城中男女三萬餘口。

translations.literal: Wei Fang briefly sent more than thirty of the surrendered men to report separately to the various Wei camps; Chen Qingzhi displayed his captives and severed heads, and with drums and shouts followed after—the nine remaining Wei cities all collapsed. Pursuing them, prisoners and heads were taken nearly to the last man; corpses choked the Wo River, and in the surrendered cities there were more than thirty thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Fang sent more than thirty of the surrendered men to report separately to the various Wei camps; Chen Qingzhi displayed his captives and severed heads and advanced with drums and shouts—the nine remaining Wei positions all collapsed. In pursuit, prisoners and heads were taken nearly to the last man; corpses choked the Wo River, and the surrendered cities yielded more than thirty thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶寅之敗於涇州也，或勸之歸罪洛陽，或曰不若留關中立功自效。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin was defeated at Jing Province, some urged him to return to Luoyang to accept punishment, others said it would be better to remain in Guanzhong and establish merit to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin was defeated at Jing Province, some urged him to return to Luoyang to accept punishment, others said it would be better to remain in Guanzhong and establish merit to redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 行台都令史河間馮景曰：「擁兵不還，此罪將大。

translations.literal: Feng Jing of Hejian, chief clerk of the forward army, said, "To hold troops and not return—this offense will be grave."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jing of Hejian, chief clerk of the forward army, said, "To hold troops and not return—this offense will be grave."

sentences.zh: 」寶寅不從，自念出師累年，糜費不貲，一旦覆敗，內不自安；

translations.literal: Baoyin would not listen; he reflected that he had campaigned for many years at immeasurable cost and had been utterly defeated in a single stroke—he was ill at ease within;
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin would not listen; he reflected that he had campaigned for many years at immeasurable cost and had been utterly defeated in a single stroke—he was ill at ease within;

sentences.zh: 魏朝亦疑之。

translations.literal: the Wei court also suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: the Wei court also suspected him.

sentences.zh: 中尉酈道元，素名嚴猛。

translations.literal: Li Daoyuan, director of the imperial guard, had always been known as stern and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daoyuan, director of the imperial guard, had always been known as stern and fierce.

sentences.zh: 司州牧汝南王悅嬖人丘念，弄權縱恣，道元收念付獄。

translations.literal: Qiu Nian, a favorite of Yuan Yue, Prince of Runan and governor of Si Province, abused power and indulged himself without restraint; Daoyuan seized Nian and handed him to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Nian, a favorite of Yuan Yue, Prince of Runan and governor of Si Province, abused power without restraint; Daoyuan seized Nian and handed him to prison.

sentences.zh: 悅請之於胡太后，太后敕赦之，道元殺之，並以劾悅。

translations.literal: Yue pleaded for him before Empress Dowager Hu; the empress dowager issued an edict to pardon him, but Daoyuan killed him anyway and also impeached Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yue pleaded for him before Empress Dowager Hu; the empress dowager issued an edict to pardon him, but Daoyuan killed him anyway and also impeached Yue.

sentences.zh: 時寶寅反狀已露，悅乃奏以道元為關右大使。

translations.literal: At this time Baoyin's rebellious designs were already exposed, and Yue memorialized to appoint Daoyuan as envoy of the Passes West.
translations.idiomatic: By then Baoyin's rebellious designs were already exposed, and Yue memorialized to appoint Daoyuan as envoy of the Passes West.

sentences.zh: 寶寅聞之，謂為取己，甚懼，長安輕薄子弟復勸使舉兵。

translations.literal: When Baoyin heard of it he thought it was aimed at seizing him and was greatly afraid; the frivolous young men of Chang'an again urged him to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin heard of it he thought it was aimed at seizing him and was greatly afraid; the frivolous young men of Chang'an again urged him to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 寶寅以問河東柳楷，楷曰：「大王，齊明帝子，天下所屬，今日之舉，實允人望。

translations.literal: Baoyin asked Liu Kai of Hedong; Kai said, "Your Highness is a son of Emperor Ming of Qi, the man to whom the realm looks—today's undertaking truly fulfills the people's hopes."
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin asked Liu Kai of Hedong; Kai said, "Your Highness is a son of Emperor Ming of Qi, the man to whom the realm looks—today's undertaking truly fulfills the people's hopes."

sentences.zh: 且謠言『鸞生十子九子毈，一子不毈關中亂。

translations.literal: "Moreover there is a saying: 'Luan bore ten sons; nine were hunchbacked, and the one who was not hunchbacked brought chaos to Guanzhong.'"
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover there is a saying: 'Luan bore ten sons; nine were hunchbacked, and the one who was not hunchbacked brought chaos to Guanzhong.'"

sentences.zh: 』亂者治也，大王當治關中，何所疑！

translations.literal: "'Chaos' means 'to govern'—Your Highness ought to govern Guanzhong; what is there to doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: "'Chaos' means 'to govern'—Your Highness ought to govern Guanzhong; what is there to doubt!"

sentences.zh: 」道元至陰盤驛，寶寅遣其將郭子恢攻殺之，收殯其屍，表言白賊所害。

translations.literal: When Daoyuan reached the Yinpan post station, Baoyin sent his general Guo Zihui to attack and kill him, gathered his corpse for burial, and memorialized that he had been killed by White rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoyuan reached the Yinpan post station, Baoyin sent his general Guo Zihui to attack and kill him, gathered his corpse for burial, and memorialized that he had been killed by White rebels.

sentences.zh: 又上表自理，稱為楊椿父子所譖。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial in his own defense, saying he had been slandered by Yang Chun and his son.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial in his own defense, saying he had been slandered by Yang Chun and his son.

sentences.zh: 寶寅行台郎中武功蘇湛，臥病在家，寶寅令湛從母弟開府屬天水姜儉說湛曰：「元略受蕭衍旨，欲見剿除。

translations.literal: Su Zhan of Wugong, a director in Baoyin's forward army, was ill at home; Baoyin had Zhan's cousin on his mother's side, Jiang Jian of Tianshui, an aide in the opener of the government office, speak to Zhan, saying, "Yuan Lue received Xiao Yan's orders and wishes to see us destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhan of Wugong, a director in Baoyin's forward army, was ill at home; Baoyin had Zhan's maternal cousin Jiang Jian of Tianshui, an aide in the opener of the government office, speak to Zhan, saying, "Yuan Lue received Xiao Yan's orders and wishes to see us destroyed."

sentences.zh: 道元之來，事不可測。

translations.literal: "Daoyuan's coming—the affair cannot be fathomed."
translations.idiomatic: "Daoyuan's coming—the affair cannot be fathomed."

sentences.zh: 吾不能坐受死亡，今須為身計，不復作魏臣矣。

translations.literal: "I cannot sit and await death; now I must plan for myself and will no longer serve as a minister of Wei."
translations.idiomatic: "I cannot sit and await death; now I must plan for myself and will no longer serve as a minister of Wei."

sentences.zh: 死生榮辱，與卿共之。

translations.literal: "Life and death, glory and shame—I share them with you."
translations.idiomatic: "Life and death, glory and shame—I share them with you."

sentences.zh: 」湛聞之，舉聲大哭。

translations.literal: When Zhan heard this he broke into loud weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan heard this he broke into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 儉遽止之，曰：「何得便爾！

translations.literal: Jian hastily stopped him and said, "How can you do this at once!"
translations.idiomatic: Jian hastily stopped him and said, "How can you weep like this!"

sentences.zh: 」湛曰：「我百口今屠滅，雲何不哭！

translations.literal: Zhan said, "My hundred mouths are to be slaughtered to the last—how can I not weep!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhan said, "My whole clan is to be slaughtered to the last—how can I not weep!"

sentences.zh: 」哭數十聲，徐謂儉曰：「為我白齊王，王本以窮鳥投入，賴朝廷假王羽翼，榮寵至此。

translations.literal: After weeping several dozen times he slowly told Jian, "Speak for me to the Prince of Qi: Your Highness came as a bird in distress seeking refuge and relied on the court to lend you wings—honor and favor reached this height."
translations.idiomatic: After weeping many times he slowly told Jian, "Speak for me to the Prince of Qi: Your Highness came as a bird in distress seeking refuge and relied on the court to lend you wings—honor and favor reached this height."

sentences.zh: 屬國步多虞，不能竭忠報德，乃欲乘人間隙，信惑行路無識之語，欲以羸敗之兵守關問鼎。

translations.literal: "When the state's fortunes are beset by many troubles you could not exhaust loyalty to repay kindness, yet now you wish to seize a human gap, trust the ignorant talk of passersby, and hold the passes with defeated troops to ask after the cauldron of rule."
translations.idiomatic: "When the state's fortunes are beset by troubles you could not exhaust loyalty to repay kindness, yet now you wish to seize an opening, trust ignorant street talk, and hold the passes with defeated troops to contest the throne."

sentences.zh: 今魏德雖衰，天命未改，且王之恩義未洽於民，但見其敗，未見有成，蘇湛不能以百口為王族滅。

translations.literal: "Now Wei's virtue may be in decline, but Heaven's mandate has not changed; moreover Your Highness's grace and righteousness have not yet reached the people—one sees only defeat, not success. Su Zhan cannot let a hundred mouths be destroyed for Your Highness's clan."
translations.idiomatic: "Now Wei's virtue may be in decline, but Heaven's mandate has not changed; moreover Your Highness's grace has not yet reached the people—one sees only defeat, not success. Su Zhan cannot let his whole clan be destroyed for Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 」寶寅復使謂曰：「我救死不得不爾，所以不先相白者，恐沮吾計耳。

translations.literal: Baoyin again sent word, saying, "To save my life I cannot but do this; the reason I did not inform you beforehand was that I feared discouraging my plan."
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin again sent word, saying, "To save my life I cannot but do this; the reason I did not inform you beforehand was that I feared discouraging my plan."

sentences.zh: 」湛曰：「凡謀大事，當得天下奇才與之從事，今但與長安博徒謀之，此有成理不？

translations.literal: Zhan said, "In plotting great affairs one ought to obtain the rare talents of the realm to undertake them with one—now you consult only with gamblers of Chang'an; is there any principle of success in this?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhan said, "In plotting great affairs one ought to obtain the rare talents of the realm to undertake them with one—now you consult only with gamblers of Chang'an; is there any principle of success in this?"

sentences.zh: 湛恐荊棘必生於齋閣，願賜骸骨歸鄉里，庶得病死，下見先人。

translations.literal: "Zhan fears thorns will surely grow in the study hall; I beg to be granted my bones to return to my home district, that I may die of illness and meet my ancestors below."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhan fears thorns will grow in the study hall; I beg leave to return home and die of illness, that I may meet my ancestors below."

sentences.zh: 」寶寅素重湛，且知其不為己用，聽還武功。

translations.literal: Baoyin had always esteemed Zhan and knew he would not serve his purposes; he allowed him to return to Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin had always esteemed Zhan and knew he would not serve his purposes; he allowed him to return to Wugong.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，寶寅自稱齊帝，改元隆緒，赦其所部，署百官。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Baoyin styled himself Emperor of Qi, changed the era name to Longxu, proclaimed amnesty within his following, and appointed the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Baoyin styled himself Emperor of Qi, changed the era name to Longxu, proclaimed amnesty within his following, and appointed the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 都督長史毛遐，鴻賓之兄也，與鴻賓帥氐、羌起兵於馬祗柵以拒寶寅；

translations.literal: Mao Xia, chief clerk to the commander and elder brother of Hongbin, joined with Hongbin in leading the Di and Qiang in revolt at Mazhi Stockade to resist Baoyin;
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xia, chief clerk to the commander and elder brother of Hongbin, joined with Hongbin in leading the Di and Qiang in revolt at Mazhi Stockade to resist Baoyin;

sentences.zh: 寶寅遣大將軍盧祖遷擊之，為遐所殺。

translations.literal: Baoyin sent the grand general Lu Zuqian to attack them, and Zuqian was killed by Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin sent the grand general Lu Zuqian to attack them, and Xia killed him.

sentences.zh: 寶寅方祀南郊，行即位禮未畢，聞敗，色變，不暇整部伍，狼狽而歸。

translations.literal: Baoyin was just then sacrificing at the southern suburb and had not finished the enthronement rites when he heard of the defeat; his countenance changed, he had no leisure to reorganize the ranks, and returned in disarray.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin was sacrificing at the southern suburb and had not finished the enthronement rites when he heard of the defeat; his countenance changed, he had no time to reorganize the ranks, and returned in disarray.

sentences.zh: 以姜儉為尚書左丞，委以心腹。

translations.literal: He made Jiang Jian Left Director among the Masters of Writing and entrusted him as a confidant.
translations.idiomatic: He made Jiang Jian Left Director among the Masters of Writing and entrusted him as a confidant.

sentences.zh: 文安周惠達為寶寅使，在洛陽，有司欲收之，惠達逃歸長安。

translations.literal: Zhou Huida of Wen'an, an envoy of Baoyin, was in Luoyang; the authorities wished to seize him, and Huida fled back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huida of Wen'an, an envoy of Baoyin, was in Luoyang; the authorities wished to seize him, and Huida fled back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 寶寅以惠達為光祿勳。

translations.literal: Baoyin made Huida Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin made Huida Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 丹陽王蕭贊聞寶寅反，懼而出走，趣白鹿山，至河橋，為人所獲，魏主知其不預謀，釋而尉之。

translations.literal: Xiao Zan, Prince of Danyang, heard that Baoyin had rebelled, was afraid, and fled toward Bailu Mountain; when he reached Heqiao he was seized by someone. The Wei sovereign knew he had not joined the plot, released him, and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zan, Prince of Danyang, heard that Baoyin had rebelled, fled in alarm toward Bailu Mountain, and was seized at Heqiao; the Wei sovereign knew he had not joined the plot, released him, and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 行台郎封偉伯等與關中豪傑謀舉兵誅寶寅，事洩而死。

translations.literal: Feng Weibo, a gentleman of the forward army, and others plotted with the powerful men of Guanzhong to raise troops and execute Baoyin; the affair was exposed and they died.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Weibo, a gentleman of the forward army, and others plotted with the powerful men of Guanzhong to raise troops and execute Baoyin; the affair was exposed and they were put to death.

sentences.zh: 魏以尚書僕射長孫稚為行台以討寶寅。

translations.literal: Wei appointed Changsun Zhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, forward-army commander to suppress Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Changsun Zhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, forward-army commander to suppress Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 正平民薛鳳賢反，宗人薛修義亦聚眾河東，分據鹽池，攻圍蒲板，東西連結以應寶寅。

translations.literal: Xue Fengxian of Zhengping rebelled; his clansman Xue Xiuyi also gathered a host in Hedong, seized the salt pools in divided occupation, attacked and besieged Puban, and linked east and west in response to Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Fengxian of Zhengping rebelled; his clansman Xue Xiuyi also gathered followers in Hedong, seized the salt pools, besieged Puban, and linked east and west in support of Baoyin.

sentences.zh: 詔都督宗正珍孫討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the commander Zongzheng Zhensun to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the commander Zongzheng Zhensun to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁卯，以護軍蕭淵藻為北討都督，鎮渦陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingmao, Xiao Yuanzao, General Who Guards the Army, was made grand commander of the northern punitive campaign and stationed at Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingmao, Xiao Yuanzao, General Who Guards the Army, was made grand commander of the northern punitive campaign and stationed at Woyang.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以渦陽置西徐州。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Western Xu Province was established at Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Western Xu Province was established at Woyang.

sentences.zh: 葛榮圍魏信都，自春及冬，冀州刺史元孚帥勵將士，晝夜拒守，糧儲既竭，外無救援，己丑，城陷；

translations.literal: Ge Rong besieged Xindu in Wei from spring through winter; Yuan Fu, governor of Ji Province, led and exhorted the officers and men in day-and-night defense. When stores were exhausted and no rescue came from outside, on jichou the city fell;
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong besieged Xindu in Wei from spring through winter; Yuan Fu, governor of Ji Province, led and exhorted the officers and men in day-and-night defense. When stores were exhausted and no rescue came from outside, on jichou the city fell;

sentences.zh: 榮執孚，逐出居民，凍死者什六七。

translations.literal: Rong seized Fu, drove out the inhabitants, and six or seven out of ten died of cold.
translations.idiomatic: Rong seized Fu, drove out the inhabitants, and six or seven out of ten died of cold.

sentences.zh: 孚兄祐為防城都督，榮大集將士，議其生死。

translations.literal: Fu's elder brother You was commander of the garrison defense; Rong assembled the officers and men in great numbers and debated their life and death.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's elder brother You was commander of the garrison defense; Rong assembled the officers and men and debated their fate.

sentences.zh: 孚兄弟各自引咎，爭相為死，都督潘紹等數百人，皆叩頭請就法以活使君。

translations.literal: The Fu brothers each took blame on himself and vied to die in the other's place; the commander Pan Shao and several hundred others all knocked their heads on the ground asking to accept punishment in order to spare the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu brothers each took blame on himself and vied to die in the other's place; the commander Pan Shao and several hundred others all knocked their heads on the ground asking to accept punishment in order to spare the governor.

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「此皆魏之忠臣義士。

translations.literal: Rong said, "These are all loyal ministers and righteous gentlemen of Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "These are all loyal ministers and righteous gentlemen of Wei."

sentences.zh: 」於是同禁者五百人皆得免。

translations.literal: Thereupon the five hundred held in the same imprisonment were all spared.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the five hundred held in the same imprisonment were all spared.

sentences.zh: 魏以源子邕為冀州刺史，將兵討榮；

translations.literal: Wei appointed Yuan Ziyong governor of Ji Province and sent troops to campaign against Rong;
translations.idiomatic: Wei appointed Yuan Ziyong governor of Ji Province and sent troops to campaign against Rong;

sentences.zh: 裴衍表請同行，詔許之。

translations.literal: Pei Yan memorialized asking to go together, and an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan memorialized asking to go together, and an edict permitted it.

sentences.zh: 子邕上言：「衍行，臣請留；

translations.literal: Ziyong submitted a memorial: "If Yan goes, I ask to remain;"
translations.idiomatic: Ziyong memorialized: "If Yan goes, I ask to remain;"

sentences.zh: 臣行，請留衍；

translations.literal: "if I go, I ask that Yan remain;"
translations.idiomatic: "if I go, I ask that Yan remain;"

sentences.zh: 若逼使同行，敗在旦夕。

translations.literal: "if we are forced to go together, defeat will come within the day."
translations.idiomatic: "if we are forced to go together, defeat will come within the day."

sentences.zh: 」不許，十二月，戊申，行至陽平東北漳水曲，榮帥眾十萬擊之，子邕、衍俱敗死。

translations.literal: This was not granted. In the twelfth month, on wushen, when they reached the bend of the Zhang River northeast of Yangping, Rong led a host of one hundred thousand to attack them, and both Ziyong and Yan were defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: This was not granted. In the twelfth month, on wushen, when they reached the bend of the Zhang River northeast of Yangping, Rong led a host of one hundred thousand to attack them, and both Ziyong and Yan were defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 相州吏民聞冀州已陷，子邕等敗，人不自保。

translations.literal: When the officials and people of Xiang Province heard that Ji Province had fallen and Ziyong and the others had been defeated, no one could protect himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the officials and people of Xiang Province heard that Ji Province had fallen and Ziyong and the others had been defeated, no one felt safe.

sentences.zh: 相州刺史恆農李神志氣自若，撫勉將士，大小致力，葛榮盡銳攻之，卒不能克。

translations.literal: Li Shen, governor of Xiang Province from Hengnong, was calm in spirit and countenance, comforted and exhorted the officers and men, and great and small gave their utmost effort; Ge Rong attacked with all his elite strength and in the end could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen, governor of Xiang Province from Hengnong, remained calm in spirit and countenance, comforted and exhorted the officers and men, and all gave their utmost; Ge Rong attacked with all his elite strength and in the end could not take it.

sentences.zh: 秦州民駱超殺杜粲，請降於魏。

translations.literal: Luo Chao of the people of Qin Province killed Du Can and asked to surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Chao of Qin Province killed Du Can and offered to surrender to Wei.
